stem: Screening for which of the following diseases must be undertaken before treatment of the thyroid carcinoma?
explanation: Pheochromocytoma screening is essential in MEN II.
case: A 22-year-old man presents to the physician›s office with the complaint of a new nodule in the neck noted 1 month ago. He is the oldest of five children ranging in age from 8 to 22. stem: Which of the following is the minimal treatment for the patient’s thyroid carcinoma?
explanation: Total thyroidectomy is the treatment for medullary carcinoma.

stem: Screening for abnormalities in which protooncogene should be offered to his siblings?
explanation: RET gene mutations are associated with MEN II.

stem: A 65-year-old woman evaluated for depression with a history of a recent kidney stone has hypercalcemia and elevated PTH. What is the most likely etiology?

multiple endocrine neoplasia type IIa (MEN IIa)
explanation: A parathyroid adenoma is the common cause in older women.

stem: An 18-year-old school student of East African origin presents with a 2-week history of lethargy, myalgia, rigours with hot flushes and intermittent pyrexia. Neither she nor any close contacts have been travelling recently. Examination reveals enlarged anterior and posterior chain lymph nodes in the neck. A blood film reveals the presence of Downey bodies, thrombocytosis and an increase in the lymphocyte count to 50% of total leucocytes. This girl is likely to have
explanation: Infectious mononucleosis is caused by Epstein–Barr virus, resulting in reactive lymphocytosis with Downey bodies; diagnosis is usually confirmed by a positive Monospot test.
_raw_ans: 60. E. Infectious mononucleosis Infectious mononucleosis is caused by Epstein–Barr virus, resulting in reactive lymphocytosis with Downey bodies; diagnosis is usually confirmed by a positive Monospot test.

stem: A 16-year-old girl presents with a smooth, round and painless lump in the midline of the neck, of which she feels very self‐conscious. On examination, it is firm, transilluminates and is painless to touch. In addition, it moves up when the patient is asked to take a sip of water. This is likely to be a
explanation: Thyroglossal cysts are remnants of the thyroglossal duct that move with swallowing and are managed by surgical excision.
_raw_ans: 61. C. Thyroglossal cyst Thyroglossal cysts are remnants of the thyroglossal duct that move with swallowing and are managed by surgical excision.

stem: A 45-year-old female business executive presents with a swelling in the midline of the neck and features of hyperthyroidism secondary to Graves’ disease. Following a course of antithyroid medication, a subtotal thyroidectomy is performed. Raised titres of which immunoglobulin would be expected in this individual?
explanation: Graves’ disease is associated with increased anti-TSH receptor antibodies.
_raw_ans: 62. E. Anti-thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibody Graves’ disease is associated with increased anti-TSH receptor antibodies.

stem: You are asked to assess a 25-year-old patient who returned from theatre 2 hours ago following a thyroidectomy for a large, hyperplastic goitre and is now complaining of difficulty swallowing sips of water. On examination you note that she is very short of breath with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths/min, using her accessory muscles of respiration and only able to answer your questions in two or three words. In addition, there appears to be a fluctuant mass in the midline of the neck underlying the surgical clips. Immediate management of this patient would be
options: Removal of surgical clips at the bedside
Intravenous access with two large-bore cannulae and fluid resuscitation
Removal of surgical clips in theatre under general anaesthesia
Call your senior and wait for him/her to remove the clips
explanation: Airway compromise from a tension hematoma post-thyroidectomy necessitates immediate bedside clip removal.
_raw_ans: 63. B. Removal of surgical clips at the bedside Airway compromise from a tension hematoma post-thyroidectomy necessitates immediate bedside clip removal.

stem: A 28-year-old secretary presents with a lump in the midline of the neck that has grown progressively larger over the past several months. On examination, there is a palpable lymph node in the left submandibular region. An aspirate is taken, confirming a malignant cancer of the thyroid gland. The origin of this is most likely to be
explanation: Papillary carcinoma is the most common thyroid cancer, often multifocal and typically spreads via lymphatics.
_raw_ans: 64. E. Papillary Papillary carcinoma is the most common thyroid cancer, often multifocal and typically spreads via lymphatics.

stem: A 37-year-old patient is diagnosed with medullary carcinoma of the thyroid gland. The concentration of which electrolyte could be reduced in this patient?
explanation: Medullary carcinoma produces calcitonin from C cells, which lowers serum calcium levels.
_raw_ans: 65. D. Calcium Medullary carcinoma produces calcitonin from C cells, which lowers serum calcium levels.

stem: A 68-year-old man presents with a 10-week history of a rapidly growing swelling in the midline of the neck. Prior to this problem developing he has been in excellent health. Over the past 10 weeks, he has begun to feel more worn out and is unable to complete his daily 3-mile walk without getting short of breath, which he was previously able to manage comfortably. His wife also reports that his voice has become increasingly hoarse in the last 2 weeks. The presentation is likely to be consistent with
explanation: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is aggressive, with rapid growth and compressive symptoms such as hoarseness and breathlessness.
_raw_ans: 66. D. Anaplastic carcinoma of the thyroid Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is aggressive, with rapid growth and compressive symptoms such as hoarseness and breathlessness.

stem: A 59-year-old fisherman presents with longstanding weight loss, anorexia and lethargy. Physical examination reveals a palpable swelling in the left supraclavicular fossa. A disseminated adenocarcinoma of the stomach is diagnosed following a gastroscopy and computed tomography scan of the thorax and abdomen. This patient has presented with
explanation: An enlarged left supraclavicular node (Troisier’s sign) suggests metastatic spread from an abdominal malignancy such as gastric adenocarcinoma.
_raw_ans: 67. D. Troisier’s sign An enlarged left supraclavicular node (Troisier’s sign) suggests metastatic spread from an abdominal malignancy such as gastric adenocarcinoma.

stem: Which of the following structures does not form a border of the anterior triangle of the neck?
explanation: The middle third of the clavicle is not included as a border of the anterior triangle of the neck.

stem: A 76-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing lump in his neck causing difficulty swallowing. Examination reveals a 4 cm hard mass in the front of the neck fixed to the overlying skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A rapidly enlarging, fixed thyroid mass in an elderly patient suggests anaplastic carcinoma.
_raw_ans: 69. A. Anaplastic carcinoma A rapidly enlarging, fixed thyroid mass in an elderly patient suggests anaplastic carcinoma.

stem: A 12-year-old girl notices a painless swelling on the left side of her neck after a recent cold. On examination, it is smooth, fluctuant, non-tender, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A painless, fluctuant swelling in the anterior triangle consistent with a branchial cyst.
_raw_ans: 70. A. Branchial cyst A painless, fluctuant swelling in the anterior triangle consistent with a branchial cyst.

stem: A 41-year-old woman presents with a 1-week history of tiredness, muscle aches, neck pain, and restlessness. On examination, she has a smooth enlarged thyroid and a heart rate of 120/min. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A painful subacute thyroiditis with transient hyperthyroid features, often viral in origin.
_raw_ans: 71. A. De Quervain thyroiditis A painful subacute thyroiditis with transient hyperthyroid features, often viral in origin.

stem: A 17-year-old boy has paroxysmal sweating, anxiety, palpitations, and a history of a thyroid tumour. He is tall and thin with long fingers. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: MEN IIb: medullary thyroid carcinoma, phaeochromocytoma, marfanoid habitus, mucosal neuromas.
_raw_ans: 72. D. Multiple endocrine neoplasia type IIb MEN IIb: medullary thyroid carcinoma, phaeochromocytoma, marfanoid habitus, mucosal neuromas.

stem: A 12-month-old girl has a large mass in the right side of her neck noticed for months. It is fleshy, compressible, and lies posterior to the sternocleidomastoid. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: A congenital lymphatic lesion in the posterior triangle of the neck, often transilluminates.
_raw_ans: 73. B. Cystic hygroma A congenital lymphatic lesion in the posterior triangle of the neck, often transilluminates.

stem: A 21-year-old man collapses after dizziness and right arm pain while sanding a table. A bony lump is palpable in the right side of his neck. Neurological and vascular exams are normal now. Most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Cervical rib compresses subclavian artery causing vertebral artery flow reversal under exertion.
_raw_ans: 74. D. Subclavian steal syndrome Cervical rib compresses subclavian artery causing vertebral artery flow reversal under exertion.

stem: A 72-year-old man presents with difficulty swallowing and regurgitation of food. He has also had several chest infections over the last few months. On examination, you see a soft swelling in the anterior triangle of the neck. On palpation, the swelling makes a gurgling sound. What is the most likely cause of his dysphagia?
explanation: A pharyngeal (Zenker) pouch can cause dysphagia, regurgitation, halitosis, and a gurgling neck swelling.
_raw_ans: 75. D. Pharyngeal pouch A pharyngeal (Zenker) pouch can cause dysphagia, regurgitation, halitosis, and a gurgling neck swelling.

stem: A 42-year-old man presents to the GP with a slowly enlarging mass in the left side of his neck which has been present for 3 months. On examination, the mass is 2 cm in diameter, non-tender, pulsatile and can be moved from side to side, but not up or down. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Carotid body tumors (chemodectomas) are pulsatile, move side to side, and lie at the bifurcation.

stem: A 36-year-old woman presents to the GP with a 2-month history of tremors. This is interfering with her work as a typist and the worry has caused her to lose over a stone in weight over the last few weeks. On examination, the thyroid appears normal although a bruit can be heard overlying it. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: An autoimmune hyperthyroidism with a diffuse goitre and bruit is classic for Graves disease.

stem: A 58-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department having been found unresponsive by her husband at home. On examination, you note that she is overweight with coarse features. explanation: Myxoedema coma requires urgent IV thyroxine and supportive care.

stem: A 32-year-old man presents to the GP with multiple lesions on his trunk which have appeared over the last few months. Each lesion is raised, firm and rubbery, and causes a tingling sensation when touched. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Benign nerve sheath tumours that can present as firm, rubbery skin lesions.
_raw_ans: 79. D. Neurofibroma Benign nerve sheath tumours that can present as firm, rubbery skin lesions.

stem: A 42-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with swelling and redness in her left cheek and malaise which has been present for 1 day. explanation: Erysipelas is a superficial streptococcal infection often managed with IV antibiotics if severe.

stem: A 46-year-old woman attends her general practice complaining of low mood and tiredness. She has had this for a few months and has had to take time off work. explanation: Spontaneous atrophic hypothyroidism with typical features of weight gain, constipation, low mood.

stem: You are called to see a 52-year-old woman who has just undergone a thyroidectomy. She complains of a 20-minute history of neck pain and shortness of breath. A rapidly expanding mass is noted around the operation site. Which of the following would you do next?

stem: A 6-year-old girl is brought to the GP by her father with a smooth lump in the midline of her neck. She is otherwise well. On examination, there is a 1 cm painless, fluctuant swelling which moves upwards on swallowing and on tongue protrusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 45-year-old woman complains to her primary care physician of nervousness, sweating, tremulousness, and weight loss. The thyroid scan shown here exhibits a pattern that is most consistent with which of the following disorders?

stem: A 35-year-old woman with a history of previous right thyroidectomy for a benign thyroid nodule now undergoes completion thyroidectomy for a suspicious thyroid mass. Administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics and debridement of the wound
Administration of high-dose steroids and antihistamines

stem: A 15-year-old otherwise healthy female high school student begins to notice galactorrhea. A pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is a frequently associated physical finding?

stem: A 52-year-old woman sees her physician with complaints of fatigue, headache, flank pain, hematuria, and abdominal pain. stem: A55-year-old woman presents with a slow-growing painless mass in her neck. stem: A55-year-old woman presents with a 6-cm right thyroid mass and palpable cervical lymphadenopathy. Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of one of the lymph nodes demonstrates the presence of thyroid tissue. Which of the following best describes the management of this thyroid disorder?
options: Screening for pancreatic endocrine neoplasms and hypercalcemia
Total thyroidectomy with modified radical neck dissection
Total thyroidectomy with frozen section intraoperatively, with modified radical neck dissection reserved for patients with extra-capsular invasion
Right thyroid lobectomy followed by iodine 131 (131I) therapy

stem: A53-year-old woman presents with complaints of weakness, anorexia, malaise, constipation, and back pain. While being evaluated, she becomes somewhat lethargic. Laboratory studies include a normal chest x-ray, serum albumin 3.2 mg/dL, serum calcium 14 mg/dL, serum phosphorus 2.6 mg/dL, serum chloride 108 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 32 mg/dL, and creatinine 2.0 mg/dL. explanation: The initial management of hypercalcemia involves intravenous normal saline to restore intravascular volume and promote renal calcium excretion.

stem: Which of the following patients with primary hyperparathyroidism should undergo parathyroidectomy?
options: A54-year-old woman with fatigue and depression
A42-year-old woman with a history of kidney stones
A59-year-old woman with mildly elevated 24-hour urinary calcium excretion
A60-year-old woman with mildly decreased bone mineral density measured at the hip of less than 2 standard deviations below peak bone density

stem: A29-year-old woman with a history of difficulty becoming pregnant presents to her primary care physician and is diagnosed with Graves disease on iodine uptake scan; her thyrotropin (TSH) level is markedly suppressed and her free thyroxine (T4) level is elevated. Preoperative treatment with phenoxybenzamine for 3 weeks
Preoperative treatment with propranolol for 1 week
No other preoperative medication is required

stem: A30-year-old woman presents with hypertension, weakness, bone pain, and a serum calcium level of 15.2 mg/dL. Plain films of bilateral hands show osteitis fibrosa cystica. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

stem: A35-year-old woman presents with a serum calcium level of 15.2 mg/ dL and an elevated parathyroid hormone level. Following correction of the patient’s hypercalcemia with hydration and furosemide, which of the following is the best therapeutic approach?

Neck exploration and resection of a parathyroid adenoma
Avoidance of sunlight, vitamin D, and calcium-containing dairy products

stem: A58-year-old man presents with tachycardia, fever, confusion, and vomiting. Workup reveals markedly elevated (triiodothyronine) T3 and (thyroxine) T4 levels. He is diagnosed as having a thyroid storm. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

Emergent radiation therapy to the neck
explanation: Thyroid storm requires immediate management with fluid replacement, antithyroid drugs, β-blockers, iodine solutions, and steroids.

stem: A34-year-old woman presents with a chief complaint of “feeling weak and thirsty as well as urinating a lot.” On presentation, her blood pressure is 165/89, heart rate is 75, and respiratory rate is 14. stem: A36-year-old woman, 20 weeks pregnant, presents with a 1.5-cm right thyroid mass. FNA is consistent with a papillary neoplasm. The mass is cold on scan and solid on ultrasound. Which of the following methods of treatment is contraindicated in this patient?
options: Total thyroidectomy with lymph node dissection
131I radioactive ablation of the thyroid gland
explanation: Radioactive iodine (131I) is contraindicated in pregnancy as it can cross the placenta and harm the fetal thyroid.

stem: A63-year-old woman notices lumps on both sides of her neck. A fine-needle aspirate is nondiagnostic, and she undergoes total thyroidectomy. Final pathology reveals a 4-cm Hürthle cell carcinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate postsurgical management of this patient?

stem: A51-year-old man presents with a 2-cm left thyroid nodule. Thyroid scan shows a cold lesion. FNA cytology demonstrates follicular cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment of this patient?

Prophylactic neck dissection is indicated along with a total thyroidectomy

stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with a history of abdominal pain and constipation. As part of her workup, she was noted to have a calcium level of 12 mg/dL. Genetic testing showing mutation in a tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 11q12-13

stem: Low 24-hour urinary calcium level (<100 mg/d)

stem: Serum calcium level 15 mg/dL and parathyroid hormone level 5 times normal

stem: A 28-year-old woman, who was hospitalized 2 months ago following a head injury, attends the outpatient clinic with a 6-week history of polyuria and polydipsia and no other symptoms. stem: During a ward round, you are asked by your surgical registrar about the management of a phaeochromocytoma. Select from the list below the most appropriate management plan for a phaeochromocytoma.

stem: A 35-year-old woman has been recently diagnosed by her GP with . Graves’ disease and has been referred to the outpatient department for further management. stem: A 50-year-old woman has had 3 weeks of pain in front of her neck. She also complains of general malaise, episodes of feeling feverish, and palpitations. stem: A 90-year-old woman has a swelling in her neck which has increased in size over the last 2 weeks. She reports difficulty in swallowing, shortness of breath, coughing, and a hoarse voice. stem: A 35-year-old woman has had a painful lump in her neck for 1 month. She has no other related symptoms. She has a solitary thyroid nodule that is slightly tender. A fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) gives a result of Thy2. Which is the single most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 40-year-old woman has undergone a total thyroidectomy for a multinodular goitre. explanation: Hormone X corresponds to Tri-iodothyronine (T3).
_raw_ans: 8. E.Tri-iodothyronine Hormone X corresponds to Tri-iodothyronine (T3).

stem: A 40-year-old man has had 1 month of spontaneous episodes of palpitations, headaches, sweating, and chest pain lasting for up to 15min. A diagnosis of phaeochromocytoma is considered. Which is the single most appropriate initial investigation that will help to confirm the diagnosis?
options: E 24h urine for vanillylmandelic acid and noradrenaline
explanation: 24h urine for vanillylmandelic acid and noradrenaline 24h urine collection for VMA and noradrenaline is the most accurate for phaeochromocytoma diagnosis.
_raw_ans: 9. E.24h urine for vanillylmandelic acid and noradrenaline 24h urine collection for VMA and noradrenaline is the most accurate for phaeochromocytoma diagnosis.

stem: A 65-year-old woman is referred by her GP following a routine blood test which showed a raised serum calcium. Over the last few months she has become constipated with intermittent bouts of abdominal pain. She is lethargic and her mood has been very low. Clinical examination is unremarkable. Biochemical results show a corrected serum calcium of 2.95mmol/L and a serum parathyroid hormone of 24pmol/L. Which is the single most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Primary hyperparathyroidism is indicated by raised calcium and PTH levels.
_raw_ans: 10. E.Primary hyperparathyroidism Primary hyperparathyroidism is indicated by raised calcium and PTH levels.

stem: A 65-year-old man has recently gained a significant amount of weight, his hair has become very dry and brittle, and his mood is low. He has a round face with a prominent fat pad along his back. Which is the single most appropriate subsequent investigation?
explanation: Clinical signs indicate Cushing’s syndrome; dexamethasone suppression test is appropriate.
_raw_ans: 11. C.Dexamethasone suppression test Clinical signs indicate Cushing’s syndrome; dexamethasone suppression test is appropriate.

items.stem: A 43-year-old man presents to his GP with a 6-month history of a painless pulsatile mass at the angle of the jaw.
items.explanation: A chemodectoma is a benign tumour of the carotid body. It presents as a pulsatile mass that moves laterally but not vertically, often with a bruit. It may secrete catecholamines and shows the ‘lyre sign’ on angiography. Treated with surgery.

items.stem: A 23-year-old girl complains of intermittent numbness and paraesthesiae in her right hand for the past 2 months. On examination there is a fixed, hard, 1 cm x 2 cm swelling in the right supraclavicular fossa.
items.explanation: A cervical rib arises from the 7th cervical vertebra and may compress neurovascular structures causing upper limb symptoms such as paraesthesia and weakness. Appears as a hard posterior neck mass.

items.stem: A 3-year-old boy is seen by his GP with an enlarging midline swelling that has been present for the past year. It is smooth and rounded, located just below the hyoid bone, measuring 2 cm x 2 cm, and rises on protrusion of the tongue.
items.explanation: A thyroglossal cyst is a midline neck mass that moves with tongue protrusion. It arises from persistent thyroglossal duct remnants. Common in children. Treated with Sistrunk’s operation.

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman presents to her GP with a neck lump enlarging for the last 3 years. It measures 1 cm x 1.5 cm and is located behind the junction of the upper and middle thirds of the left sternocleidomastoid muscle. In the past this lump has become infected, resolving with oral antibiotics.
items.explanation: A branchial cyst is a congenital neck swelling along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid. It can become infected and usually presents in young adults. Excision is the treatment.

items.stem: A 23-year-old man presents to his GP with a 2 cm x 3 cm painless lump at the angle of the jaw; it has been there for 2 months. He also complains of weight loss, night sweats and fever, over the same period. Hepatosplenomegaly is detected on examination of the abdomen.
items.explanation: Lymphoma presents as painless lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms such as weight loss and night sweats. Common in young adults. Diagnosis confirmed by biopsy and imaging.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with dysphagia and regurgitation of undigested food after about 5 minutes.
items.explanation: Pharyngeal pouch typically presents with dysphagia and regurgitation of undigested food several minutes after eating, often in elderly men.

items.stem: A 75-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of increasing dysphagia to solids, pain on swallowing and weight loss.
items.explanation: Hypopharyngeal carcinoma can cause progressive dysphagia, odynophagia, and weight loss in elderly patients.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of a sensation of a lump in the throat. There is no dysphagia and the sensation improves when she swallows.
items.explanation: Globus pharyngeus is a sensation of a lump in the throat without true dysphagia, often improves with swallowing and is linked to anxiety or reflux.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with a gradually increasing swelling in the lower part of the neck. Occasionally food can ‘stick’ when swallowed. The swelling was found to move on swallowing.
items.explanation: Thyroid goitre can compress the oesophagus causing intermittent dysphagia; moves with swallowing.

items.stem: A 75-year-old man wakes up in the middle of the night with sudden onset of pain in the neck and difficulty swallowing his saliva. He has no symptoms during the day.
items.explanation: Foreign body impaction may cause sudden nocturnal onset of neck pain and difficulty swallowing, especially with saliva, indicating acute obstruction.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with a lump on the scalp. Examination reveals a smooth, spherical tense lump. A small punctum can be seen on the surface.
items.explanation: The small punctum seen on the scalp lump indicates a blocked sebaceous gland, which is typical of a sebaceous cyst; the lesion’s smooth, spherical, and tense nature further supports this diagnosis.,

items.stem: A 33-year-old man presents with a swelling on the upper arm which has been growing slowly for a number of years. Examination reveals a soft, compressible, non-tender lobulated mass.
items.explanation: The slow-growing, soft, compressible, and lobulated mass in the arm is consistent with a lipoma – a benign tumor composed of fat cells that typically presents as a painless and mobile swelling.,

items.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless swelling on the dorsum of the right hand. Examination reveals a smooth, spherical, tense, 1.5-cm swelling. The overlying skin can be drawn over it.
items.explanation: The painless, mobile, and tense swelling on the dorsum of the hand, with skin that can be drawn over it, is characteristic of a ganglion, which commonly arises near joints or tendon sheaths.,

items.stem: A 29-year-old man presents with two mobile fusiform-shaped lumps on the forearm. Each swelling feels like firm rubber and causes tingling in the hand upon pressure.
items.explanation: The mobile, fusiform, rubbery lumps on the forearm that cause tingling on pressure suggest a neurofibroma, a benign nerve sheath tumor that can produce neurologic symptoms due to its association with peripheral nerves.,

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with a rapidly growing lump just below the eye. Examination reveals a 2-cm, smooth, round, skin-coloured lump with a black central core. The lump is freely mobile over subcutaneous tissues.
items.explanation: The rapidly growing, smooth, round lesion just below the eye with a central black core is indicative of a keratoacanthoma, a skin lesion that grows quickly and often features a central keratin plug.

items.stem: A 75-year-old woman presents with acute airway obstruction and a thyroid mass after several weeks of worsening shortness of breath. Postmortem reveals a thyroid mass that has invaded the trachea and surrounding structures. Histology shows giant cells containing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei.
items.explanation: An elderly patient with rapid airway obstruction, invasive thyroid mass and giant pleomorphic cells on histology indicates anaplastic carcinoma, which is aggressive and locally invasive.;

items.stem: A 38-year-old patient presents with a 2.5-cm right-sided thyroid mass. On examination there is mild enlargement of the cervical lymph nodes. A thyroidectomy is performed and histology reveals a non-encapsulated infiltrative mass. Psammoma bodies and epithelial cells with large clear areas within the nuclei are noted.
items.explanation: A middle‐aged patient presenting with a thyroid mass exhibiting psammoma bodies and clear nuclear features with cervical lymphadenopathy is classic for papillary carcinoma.;

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with a diffusely enlarged thyroid gland. On examination she has a fine tremor and exophthalmos.
items.explanation: A young woman with diffuse thyroid enlargement accompanied by tremor and exophthalmos points to Graves’ disease, an autoimmune hyperthyroid condition affecting both the thyroid and orbital tissues.;

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with a tender thyroid swelling associated with fever. Investigations reveal no evidence of infection.
items.explanation: A patient with a tender thyroid swelling and fever, without signs of infection elsewhere, suggests de Quervain’s thyroiditis, a subacute granulomatous inflammation usually following a viral illness.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman presents with a history of increasing weight gain, tiredness and neck swelling. On examination the patient has a firm rubbery goitre. Fine-needle aspiration shows a diffuse lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate. The report also mentions the presence of lymphoid follicles and parenchymal atrophy.
items.explanation: Hashimoto’s disease: A 36‐year-old woman with weight gain, tiredness and a firm, rubbery goitre; FNA demonstrating diffuse lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrates with lymphoid follicles and parenchymal atrophy is typical of chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with a history of a slowly growing right-sided lump at the base of the neck. On examination there is a thyroid nodule with associated lymphadenopathy. She has a recent history of adrenalectomy.
items.explanation: Medullary carcinoma: A 40‐year-old woman with a thyroid nodule, lymphadenopathy and a history of adrenalectomy (suggesting MEN2 syndrome) points to medullary carcinoma.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a painless, firm, left-sided neck swelling. Fine-needle aspiration reveals the presence of multiple compact follicles. Histology shows evidence of capsular and blood vessel invasion.
items.explanation: Follicular carcinoma: A 45‐year-old woman with a firm thyroid swelling showing multiple compact follicles and, on histology, evidence of capsular and vascular invasion is diagnostic of follicular carcinoma.

items.stem: A 55-year-old African man is referred to the ENT clinic with a large, smooth goitre that has been increasing in size for at least 20 years.
items.explanation: Endemic goitre: A 55‐year-old man with a long-standing (20 years) large, smooth goitre is consistent with an iodine deficiency–induced endemic goitre.

items.stem: A 1-year-old boy is brought to general practice by his mother with a large mass in his neck that has been present for a while. On examination, the mass is located posterior to the left sternocleidomastoid muscle. It is soft, compressible, and transilluminates.
items.explanation: Cystic hygroma is a congenital lymphatic malformation in the posterior triangle that transilluminates.

items.stem: A 64-year-old woman presents with a rapidly growing mass in her neck associated with drooping of the right side of her face. On examination, there is a 4 cm hard mass in the neck that is attached to the overlying skin.
items.explanation: Rapid growth and skin fixation suggest salivary duct carcinoma.

items.stem: A 13-year-old boy presents with a painless neck lump on the left side. On examination, there is a 2 cm lump at the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid that is smooth and fluctuant but does not transilluminate.
items.explanation: Branchial cyst is a fluctuant mass along the anterior border of SCM.

items.stem: An 8-year-old girl presents with a smooth lump in the midline of the neck. On examination, there is a 1 cm painless, fluctuant swelling in the midline that moves upward on swallowing and with tongue protrusion.
items.explanation: Movement with swallowing and tongue protrusion confirms thyroglossal cyst.

items.stem: A 56-year-old man presents to the emergency department with pain and swelling in his neck that occurs every time he eats and lasts around an hour. He has experienced this for over a fortnight. On examination, there is no obvious swelling or erythema.
items.explanation: Pain on eating indicates a salivary gland stone obstructing the duct.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman attends her general practice complaining of low mood and lethargy. She has had this for a few months and has missed much time at work. On further questioning, she admits to being constipated and to having gained weight. On examination, no abnormality is apparent in the neck and no lymphadenopathy is palpable.
items.explanation: Hypothyroid symptoms of lethargy, constipation, and weight gain indicate primary myxoedema.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman goes to her general practitioner following a sudden, sharp pain in her neck earlier in the day. Since then, she has found it difficult to breathe. On examination, you find a swelling on the right side of her neck. The patient tells you that this swelling has been there for some time and has never previously caused her any trouble.
items.explanation: Sudden pain in a pre-existing thyroid nodule suggests haemorrhage into a cyst.

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman presents with a 5-week history of resting tremor and diarrhoea. She mentions that just before these symptoms occurred, she had some time off work with a cough and cold. On examination, her pulse is 96/min and regular. The thyroid gland is generally enlarged and slightly tender to touch. No cervical lymph nodes are palpable.
items.explanation: Tender enlarged thyroid after viral illness indicates de Quervain thyroiditis.

items.stem: A 22-year-old anxious woman presents to her general practitioner with a month’s history of worsening diarrhoea. On further questioning, she admits losing 10 pounds over the last few weeks despite having a good appetite. On examination, you notice a slight tremor, her pulse is 110/min and irregular, and a bruit is heard over the thyroid, though there is no obvious deformity or palpable nodes. although a bruit is heard over the thyroid
items.explanation: Weight loss, tachycardia, tremor, and thyroid bruit are characteristic of Graves disease.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman is brought by her husband to the emergency department with reduced consciousness. On examination, she has a temperature of 30°C and her pulse is 48/min. Her husband tells you that she has a history of depression and has recently been refusing to take her regular medications.
items.explanation: Severe hypothermia, bradycardia, and altered consciousness in untreated hypothyroidism indicate myxoedema coma.

items.stem: A 25-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a slowly enlarging lump on the left side of her neck. She denies any other symptoms. On examination, there is a 2 cm smooth, regular, firm lump that moves up with swallowing but not with tongue protrusion. Lymph nodes are palpable on the left side of the neck.
items.explanation: Papillary carcinoma presents as a firm painless nodule in young women.

items.stem: A 54-year-old man presents to clinic with a midline neck mass that has been increasing in size over a few months. On examination, the thyroid gland is enlarged, firm, and irregular, although the patient does not complain of any pain. No cervical nodes are palpable. A core biopsy is taken and the histology report denies the presence of malignancy.
items.explanation: Riedel thyroiditis causes a fibrotic goitre with benign histology.

items.stem: A 42-year-old woman presents to her general practitioner with a long-standing goitre. More recently, she has been suffering with constipation, lethargy, and weight gain. On examination, her pulse is 64/min and regular. She has a diffusely enlarged, smooth, firm goitre. No lymph nodes are palpable.
items.explanation: Hashimoto thyroiditis presents with a firm goitre and hypothyroid symptoms.

items.stem: A 46-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with palpitations. She is clearly nervous and describes having multiple paroxysms of fast palpitations over the preceding fortnight. On examination, you find an enlarged, lumpy thyroid gland that is not fixed to the overlying skin.
items.explanation: Toxic multinodular goitre causes hyperthyroid symptoms with nodular enlargement.

items.stem: An 84-year-old woman presents with a lump in her neck that was first noticed last month and has since been growing rapidly. On further questioning, she admits to problems swallowing her food. On examination, there is a 5 cm irregular, hard mass on the left side that is fixed to the overlying skin.
items.explanation: Anaplastic carcinoma is an aggressive thyroid cancer in the elderly.

items.stem: A 30-year-old man has had a lump on the right side of his neck for years which intermittently discharges. There is a superficial, mobile lump in the posterior triangle with a visible punctum.
items.explanation: Sebaceous cysts are common, superficial, mobile, and have a central punctum.

items.stem: A 20-year-old man has an asymptomatic swelling just to the right of midline in the anterior neck. It feels firm and moves on tongue protrusion.
items.explanation: Thyroglossal cysts move with tongue protrusion and lie near midline.

items.stem: A 15-year-old boy has a smooth, non-tender, fluctuant mass along the lower anteromedial border of the sternocleidomastoid. It occasionally increases in size, causing discomfort.
items.explanation: Branchial cysts occur along the anterior border of SCM and are fluctuant.

items.stem: A 50-year-old man has a soft, mobile, non-tender lump in the left anterior triangle and several smaller similar lumps on the right.
items.explanation: Lipomas are soft, mobile, painless fatty tumours; can be multiple.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman has an enlarging left-sided neck swelling, 9 kg weight loss, lethargy, and a diffuse, rubbery, firm mass in the left anterior triangle with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy.
items.explanation: Lymphoma presents with rubbery lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms.

stem: A 36-year-old multiparous woman attends your clinic with a 7-day history of left breast pain after being involved in a car accident. On examining her breast, you notice a 3-cm hard, irregular, immobile, and tender lump. You also notice some skin tethering and overlying bruising at the region of the lump. Ultrasound features suggest a benign pathology. The most likely diagnosis at this point is:
explanation: Ultrasound features indicate benign pathology.
_raw_ans: 1. A. Fat necrosis. Ultrasound features indicate benign pathology.

stem: A 32-year-old woman came to the breast clinic with five weeks history of redness and swelling around the right nipple. There is no past medical history but she is a heavy smoker. On examination, there is peri-areolar skin inflammation with a small palpable tender mass just behind the nipple. The most likely diagnosis is:
explanation: Presentation and smoking history indicate peri-ductal mastitis.
_raw_ans: 2. B. Peri-ductal mastitis Presentation and smoking history indicate peri-ductal mastitis.

stem: A 36-year-old woman complains of a 3-month history of bloody discharge from the nipple. On examination, a small nodule is found deep to the areola. Careful palpation of the nipple-areola complex results in blood appearing at one duct. Mammogram findings are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Bloody discharge with a nodule suggests intraductal papilloma.
_raw_ans: 3. A. Intraductal papilloma Bloody discharge with a nodule suggests intraductal papilloma.

sub: Bailey Breast and Neck lumps MCQ
stem: Which of the following statements are true? (Benign Breast Disease)
options: Nipple retraction always indicates an underlying malignancy.
Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause for lactational mastitis.
Fibroadenomas should always be offered excision, as they are associated with a high risk of malignancy.
The histology of phyllodes tumour may be benign, intermediate or malignant.
Blood-stained nipple discharge is usually due to a breast carcinoma.
explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the usual cause of lactational mastitis and phyllodes tumours may be benign, intermediate or malignant.
_raw_ans: 4. B. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause for lactational mastitis., D. The histology of phyllodes tumour may be benign, intermediate or malignant. Staphylococcus aureus is the usual cause of lactational mastitis and phyllodes tumours may be benign, intermediate or malignant.

stem: A 51-year-old woman presents with a 2-month history of right breast blood-tinged nipple discharge from a single duct; mammogram is negative, cytology is non-diagnostic, ductogram shows a solitary filling defect. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: intraductal papilloma Solitary papilloma is the most common cause of pathologic nipple discharge in one duct.
_raw_ans: 5. C) intraductal papilloma Solitary papilloma is the most common cause of pathologic nipple discharge in one duct.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management for the intraductal papilloma?
options: (A) collection of discharge for repeat cytologic analysis
(B) observation, with repeat examination and imaging in 3–6 months
(D) central lumpectomy (including removal of the nipple/areolar complex)
explanation: terminal duct excision (microdochectomy) Definitive diagnosis and treatment by excision of the involved duct.
_raw_ans: 6. E) terminal duct excision (microdochectomy) Definitive diagnosis and treatment by excision of the involved duct.

stem: A 25-year-old woman presents with right breast pain localized to the nipple areolar complex with a subareolar fluid collection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Presentation is consistent with periductal mastitis.
_raw_ans: 7. B. periductal mastitis with abscess Presentation is consistent with periductal mastitis.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management of the breast mass?
options: aspiration of the fluid and antibiotics
central lumpectomy, axillary node dissection, and radiation therapy
antibiotics alone with re-evaluation in 1 week
explanation: Management of periductal mastitis with abscess involves aspiration and antibiotics.
_raw_ans: 8. A. aspiration of the fluid and antibiotics Management of periductal mastitis with abscess involves aspiration and antibiotics.

stem: A 33-year-old woman with a 2-month left breast mass that is firm, mobile, and well-defined is most consistent with?
explanation: The features most closely match a fibroadenoma.
_raw_ans: 9. D. fibroadenoma The features most closely match a fibroadenoma.

stem: What management is recommended for the above breast mass?
options: re-examination after the next menstrual cycle
explanation: Needle biopsy is advised to confirm the diagnosis.
_raw_ans: 10. C. needle biopsy Needle biopsy is advised to confirm the diagnosis.

stem: A 55-year-old man with known atrial fibrillation presents to his general practitioner with a 3-month history of gynaecomastia. Which of his following medications is not associated with gynaecomastia?
explanation: Furosemide is not typically associated with gynaecomastia, unlike the other medications listed.
_raw_ans: 11. D. Furosemide Furosemide is not typically associated with gynaecomastia, unlike the other medications listed.

stem: A worried 23-year-old woman, who started taking the combined contraceptive pill 3 months ago, presents with a 1-day history of discovering a painless lump in the right breast. The patient states that the lump was not there a month ago. On examination, a slightly mobile, discrete, well‐defined, non‐tender, firm 1 cm diameter lump is found. There is no lymphadenopathy. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: Fibroadenomas typically occur in young women presenting as painless, mobile, firm lumps, differentiating them from cysts, lipomas, and carcinomas.
_raw_ans: 12. C. Fibroadenoma Fibroadenomas typically occur in young women presenting as painless, mobile, firm lumps, differentiating them from cysts, lipomas, and carcinomas.

stem: A 36-year-old nulliparous woman attends your clinic with a 7-day history of left breast pain after being involved in a car accident. On examining her breast, you notice a hard, irregular 3 cm, immobile, tender lump. You also notice some skin tethering and overlying bruising in the region of the lump. Ultrasound features suggest a benign pathology. The most likely diagnosis at this point is
explanation: Recent trauma with bruising and tenderness indicates fat necrosis rather than carcinoma or other pathology.
_raw_ans: 13. A. Fat necrosis Recent trauma with bruising and tenderness indicates fat necrosis rather than carcinoma or other pathology.

stem: A 33-year-old, non-smoking, breastfeeding woman is 10 days postpartum. She has a 4-day history of a slight crack on the surface of her left nipple. She presents with a 2-day history of severe continuous pain in the left breast, spiking pyrexia up to 38.8 with rigours which has prevented her from sleeping. On examination, you find the outer quadrants of the left breast to be red, warm and tender with a hard 3 cm lump at the edge of the left nipple. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: In a lactating woman with a nipple crack and severe localized pain, the findings favor a breast abscess over other conditions.
_raw_ans: 14. D. Breast abscess In a lactating woman with a nipple crack and severe localized pain, the findings favor a breast abscess over other conditions.

stem: A 43-year-old woman presents to your clinic with a 2-month history of localized dull pain in the right breast. The pain intensifies just before her period. On examination, you find a discrete 2.5 cm mobile, tense, tender, fluctuant lump in the lower inner quadrant of the right breast. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: A mobile, fluctuant lump in a woman over 40 suggests a benign breast cyst.
_raw_ans: 15. C. Breast cyst A mobile, fluctuant lump in a woman over 40 suggests a benign breast cyst.

stem: A 47-year-old perimenopausal woman presents with a 3-week history of green discharge from the right nipple. On examination, the right nipple is non-tender, has a ‘slit-like’ appearance and is retracted. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: The slit-like nipple with green discharge in a perimenopausal woman points to mammary duct ectasia.
_raw_ans: 16. D. Mammary duct ectasia The slit-like nipple with green discharge in a perimenopausal woman points to mammary duct ectasia.

stem: A 25-year-old woman presents to your clinic after discovering, for the first time, two lumps in the inner lower quadrant of her left breast. On examination you find these lumps to be 2 cm in size, solid, discrete, mobile and non-tender. The right breast is normal and there is no lymphadenopathy. The most appropriate course of management is
options: Reassure the patient and discharge her
Request an ultrasound of the left breast
explanation: In a 25-year-old with new breast lumps, ultrasound is the most appropriate next step in triple assessment.
_raw_ans: 17. C. Request an ultrasound of the left breast In a 25-year-old with new breast lumps, ultrasound is the most appropriate next step in triple assessment.

stem: A 21-year-old nulliparous woman presents to your clinic with a 1-month history of bilateral breast pain. The pain, which is dull and achy in nature, is poorly localized and widespread across both breasts. The pain gradually increases in severity and is worse just before her menses. The pain usually starts to get better once her menses start. On examination, both breasts are tender. There are no lumps, skin changes or obvious swellings. The most likely diagnosis here is
explanation: Bilateral breast pain that worsens premenstrually is characteristic of cyclical mastalgia.
_raw_ans: 18. C. Cyclical mastalgia Bilateral breast pain that worsens premenstrually is characteristic of cyclical mastalgia.

stem: A 25-year-old woman is diagnosed with a 1.5 cm palpable area of fat necrosis of the left breast by core biopsy following a traumatic injury 14 days earlier. She has slight bruising of the lower outer quadrant of the left breast with moderate tenderness. What would be the most appropriate course of management?
options: Follow-up appointment for ultrasound in 3 months
Follow-up appointment for ultrasound in 6 months
explanation: Traumatic fat necrosis usually resolves without intervention, thus reassurance and discharge is appropriate.
_raw_ans: 19. A. Reassurance and discharge Traumatic fat necrosis usually resolves without intervention, thus reassurance and discharge is appropriate.

stem: A 38-year-old woman, and mother of two healthy children, is diagnosed with a fluid-filled simple cyst after triple assessment. On ultrasound the inner surface of the cyst looks entirely smooth. The woman does not have any significant family history of carcinoma and the cyst is located in the outer-lower quadrant of the right breast. What would be the most appropriate course of action?
explanation: Benign breast cysts are managed with annual follow-up after benign imaging findings.
_raw_ans: 20. C. Annual follow–up Benign breast cysts are managed with annual follow-up after benign imaging findings.

stem: A 30-year-old woman who is 12 days postpartum and breastfeeding is diagnosed with acute mastitis of the left breast. Four days earlier, she discovered a painful crack in the region of the left nipple and noticed that the surrounding skin was tender, warm and red in colour. The patient is not allergic to penicillin and you decide to prescribe a course of antibiotics. What would be the most appropriate antibiotic for treating this condition?
explanation: In a breastfeeding woman with acute mastitis, flucloxacillin is the treatment of choice.
_raw_ans: 21. D. Flucloxacillin In a breastfeeding woman with acute mastitis, flucloxacillin is the treatment of choice.

stem: After a triple assessment, including core biopsy, a 28-year-old woman is diagnosed with a fibroadenoma of the left breast. The patient has a significant family history of breast carcinoma. The non-tender lump is situated in the inner lower quadrant of the left breast. The lump is approximately 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm. What is the most appropriate course of management?
options: The patient should be given the choice of excision or not and if not she could be discharged
Perform triple assessment again in 6 weeks
explanation: Due to family history of breast cancer, excision of the fibroadenoma is appropriate.
_raw_ans: 22. A. Excision of the lump Due to family history of breast cancer, excision of the fibroadenoma is appropriate.

stem: A 45-year-old perimenopausal woman is diagnosed with mammary duct ectasia of the right breast after having had small and infrequent amounts of milky green discharge from multiple ducts of the right nipple for over 2 months. The patient has no significant family history and mammography findings are normal. What is the most appropriate course of management?
options: Surgical resection of the duct system of the right breast (Hadfield’s operation)
Perform mammography of the right breast in 3 months
explanation: Normal findings in mammary duct ectasia warrant reassurance and discharge.
_raw_ans: 23. A. Reassure and discharge Normal findings in mammary duct ectasia warrant reassurance and discharge.

stem: A 48-year-old perimenopausal woman presents with a 2-month history of a painful lump in her right breast. On examination you find a 2.5 cm tense, fluctuant, mobile lump in the outer lower quadrant of the right breast. The most appropriate next course of action is
explanation: In a woman over 35, combined mammography and ultrasound is the appropriate next step.
_raw_ans: 24. B. Mammography and ultrasound In a woman over 35, combined mammography and ultrasound is the appropriate next step.

stem: A 34-year-old premenopausal woman presents to your clinic with a lump in her right breast. On examination you find a 2.5 cm fluctuant, mobile, tender lump in the inner lower quadrant of the right breast. The ultrasound report suggests a benign fluid-filled cyst. The most appropriate course of action is
explanation: For a benign cystic lesion on ultrasound, fine needle aspiration is the next appropriate step.
_raw_ans: 25. B. Ultrasound guided fine needle aspiration For a benign cystic lesion on ultrasound, fine needle aspiration is the next appropriate step.

stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with multiple bilateral breast swellings which cause discomfort, particularly just before her periods. They have been present for several years but appear to be getting worse. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Multiple painful nodular changes related to menstrual cycle are characteristic of fibrocystic disease.
_raw_ans: 26. D. Fibrocystic disease Multiple painful nodular changes related to menstrual cycle are characteristic of fibrocystic disease.

stem: A 38-year-old woman presents with subareolar pain in the left breast and occasional blood-stained nipple discharge. Examination is unremarkable. What is the most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 27-year-old woman presents with a single lump in the left breast that has been present for 6 months. On examination, there is a 3 cm smooth lump in the upper outer quadrant, mobile and not attached to the skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 28-year-old woman comes to see you at the GP practice having noticed a lump in the right breast. She is concerned that it may be cancer. Refer the patient for urgent mammography
Refer the patient for urgent ultrasound scan

stem: A 22-year old woman presents to the GP complaining of a 2-week history of milky discharge from both her breasts. She is otherwise well. stem: A 40-year-old woman has had 3 weeks of unilateral breast pain. The pain has been constant with no relation to her menstrual cycle. stem: A 50-year-old woman has had intermittent nipple discharge. She has noticed that the discharge seems to be coming from one point on the left nipple. The discharge is slightly blood-stained. stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a unilateral erythematous, itchy rash around her nipple and inversion of the nipple. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 35-year-old woman has a lump in the upper outer quadrant of her right breast that becomes tender pre-menses. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 31-year-old woman has a nontender, rubbery, mobile lump in her left breast. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 67-year-old woman 2 weeks post breast-conserving surgery notices a painless lump beneath the incision, nontender, firm, well-circumscribed. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 35-year-old woman has a tense, mobile breast lump that yields straw-coloured fluid on fine-needle aspiration. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A middle-aged woman has a serous discharge from one nipple on deep palpation. The breast otherwise appears normal. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 28-year-old woman has a discrete tense, mobile breast lump suspicious of a cyst. Which investigation is most appropriate?

stem: A 52-year-old woman has a large painless breast lump, fleshy with a tear-drop shape. Most likely diagnosis?

stem: A 42-year-old female underwent radical mastectomy with axillary clearance. At her first follow-up, the inferior angle of her ipsilateral scapula translocates medially with any attempt at overhead activity. Injury to which of the following structures would most likely cause this abnormality?

stem: A 56-year-old woman presents to the physician’s office with complaints of a new left breast mass. She denies any pain, nipple discharge, or skin dimpling. stem: A 56-year-old woman presents to the clinic for routine health screening. She is concerned about the development of breast cancer. stem: A 42-year-old woman returns to the clinic following an uneventful biopsy for a well-defined, mobile mass. stem: A 35-year-old woman with a strong family history of breast cancer (including a sister with a deleterious BRCA1 mutation) is found to carry the same mutation. stem: A 70-year-old woman has had a lump in her left breast for 12 months. This lump has gradually increased in size and she has recently noticed that the shape of her breast has changed. stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with a lump in the left breast. Her family history is negative for breast cancer. On examination the mass is rubbery, mobile, and nontender to palpation. explanation: Lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS) is considered a risk factor for invasive breast carcinoma and is managed with frequent self-exams and yearly mammograms.
