It is the gold standard test for eradication of H pylori
A 24 years old male with multiple perioral bluish-black pigmented lesions is presented with multiple ileal and colonic polyps.
items.explanation: Hammartamatous polyp Hammartamatous polyps are associated with syndromes such as Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome, which presents with characteristic pigmented lesions and multiple polyps in the gastrointestinal tract.

items.stem: A 28 years old male with hundreds of polyps in his rectum and colon
A 45 years old male with a history of ulcerative colitis, is found to have multiple pseudopolyps on endoscopy.
items.explanation: Inflammatory polyps can be seen in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including ulcerative colitis. These polyps are not precancerous.

items.stem: Commonest polyp in children and adolescents.
items.explanation: Hyperplastic polyps are commonly seen in the younger population and are typically small and benign.

items.stem: This type of polyps carries a high risk of malignant transformation.
items.explanation: Villous adenomatous polyps have a higher risk of malignant transformation compared to other types of polyps.

items.stem: A 25-year-old mature student decides to enter a drug trial to fund his education. Routine blood tests on admission show an elevated bilirubin concentration in the absence of any other abnormality
items.explanation: Elevated bilirubin concentration in the absence of any other abnormality suggests an excessive breakdown of red blood cells, leading to an increased production of unconjugated bilirubin. This can occur in conditions such as hemolytic anemia or Gilbert’s syndrome.

items.stem: A 39-year-old man develops jaundice after commencing rifampicin and isoniazid for tuberculosis.
items.explanation: The use of rifampicin and isoniazid for tuberculosis treatment can cause drug-induced liver injury, leading to hepatocellular damage and subsequent jaundice.

items.stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with right upper quadrant pain, nausea and jaundice. On further questioning, she admits to having pale stools and dark urine.
items.explanation: The symptoms of right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and jaundice, along with pale stools and dark urine, suggest an obstruction of the bile flow, commonly seen in conditions such as choledocholithiasis.

items.stem: Patient with a known history of ulcerative colitis presents with jaundice
items.explanation: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), a condition characterized by inflammation and scarring of the bile ducts within the liver, most commonly occurs with ulcerative colitis.

items.stem: A 23 years old female is found to be HCV Ab +ve on regular checkup for breast lump surgery. The best treatment now is:
A 23 years old male is found to have a perforated appendicitis during surgery for acute abdomen. The best antibiotic option would be:
A 27 years old male with history of restorative proctocolectomy is enduring recurrent attacks of pouchitis. The best treatment in addition to lactobacillus is:
A 34 years old male has persistent H. pylori infection in spite of multiple eradication regimes. In combination with pantoprazole, the next 2nd line regime is:
A 43 years old alcoholic male presents with sudden excruciating upper abdominal pain radiating to back. CT scan shows fluid in lesser sac with enlarged pancreas. The best treatment now is:
Although it is classified as 2nd generation cephalosporin, it has an anaerobic activity.
CA colon
items.explanation: Elevated levels of Carcinoembryonic may indicate the presence of colorectal cancer

items.stem: CA pancreas
items.explanation: Elevated levels of CA 19-9 may indicate the presence of pancreatic cancer, but it can also be elevated in other conditions such as cholangiocarcinoma and some benign diseases.

items.stem: HCC (Hepatocellular carcinoma)
items.explanation: Alpha fetoprotein is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma

items.stem: A 37-year-old lady with a history of left parotid tumor is presented with a left preauricular lump 2 years after she had surgery to remove it. FNAC shows epithelial and stromal cells.
items.explanation: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign tumor of the salivary glands, and the parotid gland is the most commonly affected site. It is characterized by a mixture of epithelial and stromal components.

items.stem: A 54-year-old lady with a history of joint problem is presented with dry mouth and dry red eyes. Examination revealed non-tender mild enlargement of both parotid glands.
items.explanation: Sjogren’s syndrome is an autoimmune disorder that primarily affects the salivary and lacrimal glands, leading to decreased tear and saliva production. It commonly presents with dry mouth (xerostomia) and dry eyes (keratoconjunctivitis sicca).

items.stem: A 67-year-old male is on parenteral nutrition for 3 weeks, because of serious abdominal trauma in an RTA. He complains of a painful left lump below his left jaw, with a fever. Examination shows bad oral hygiene, with teeth caries. WBC count is 14,000/mm³.
items.explanation: The patient’s symptoms of a painful lump below the left jaw, along with fever and bad oral hygiene, are indicative of an infection in the salivary gland.

items.stem: A 68-year-old male is presented with bilateral parotid enlargement. FNAC shows neoplastic epithelial cells and lymphocytes.
items.explanation: Warthin’s tumor, also known as papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum, is a benign tumor that commonly affects the parotid gland. It is characterized by bilateral parotid gland enlargement and the presence of neoplastic epithelial cells and lymphocytes on fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC). It is common in older males.

items.stem: A 25-year-old patient presents with diarrhea, weight loss, and a lump near the midline.
items.explanation: Chronic diarrhea, weight loss and lump suggests Crohn’s disease.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man with a positive history of surgery and a right iliac fossa scar.
items.explanation: The presence of a surgical scar in the right iliac fossa and the clinical history of surgery suggests a possible complication related to the appendix.

items.stem: A 65-year-old male presents with weight loss and bloody stool. On examination, a pale face and a non-tender right iliac fossa mass are noted.
items.explanation: Elderly + weight loss + bleeding per rectum + RIF mass => Cancer.

items.stem: A patient presenting with multiple discharging sinuses four weeks after appendectomy surgery.
items.explanation: The presentation of multiple sinuses following an appendectomy surgery suggests the possibility of abdominal actinomycosis.

items.stem: A patient presents with fever, sweating, itching, and hepatosplenomegaly.
items.explanation: Fever, sweating (especially night sweats), and itching (pruritus) are known as ‘B symptoms’ and are characteristic features of lymphoma. Hepatosplenomegaly is also frequently observed in lymphoma

items.stem: A patient with a history of an empty scrotum for many years presents with a lump in the right iliac fossa.
Abnormal veins are seen in the lower end of the oesophagus, which are dilated and grape like.
items.explanation: Barrett’s oesophagus This is becoming increasingly important, as it is associated with increasing the risk of malignancy. The incidence of adenocarinoma of the lower end of the oesophagus is increasing. Barrett’s oesophagus showing dysplastic changes needs regular surveillance. There is still some debate about its management, but most agree that severe dysplastic changes would be a strong reason for surgery. Invasive carcinoma may be found in almost half of these cases.

items.stem: A smooth, tapering stricture is seen at the lower end of the oesophagus along with inflammation and ulceration.
items.explanation: Carcinoma of the oesophagus This causes profound weight loss and rapidly progressive dysphagia. Staging investigations such as endoscopic US, computerised tomography (CT) scan and laparoscopy are important before embarking on major resections. Prognosis still remains poor.

items.stem: A mucosal tear is seen at the cardia with some fresh blood.
items.explanation: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) This may be an incidental finding but can cause upper gastrointestinal bleed, which draws attention. Prognosis, though variable, is a lot better than adenocarcinoma. Even advanced cases respond to tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib.

items.stem: The pylorus is seen to be wide open with plenty of bile in the stomach. The antrum shows streaks of erythema.
items.explanation: Hiatus hernia A small hiatus hernia may be an incidental finding. Some are associated with features of reflux oesophagitis. This can rarely present with complications such as incarceration, necrosis and perforation.

items.stem: The stomach is difficult to distend and appears to have low capacity. The mucosa appears stretched but no mucosal lesion is seen.
items.explanation: The mucosa may appear deceptively normal (though a bit stretched) and biopsies may be negative because the pathology is submucosal. The stomach will be very contracted and non- distensible. Special biopsy forceps are necessary to get the required tissue. Patients usually present late and hence this carries a very poor prognosis.

items.stem: A submucosal lump is seen. The mucosa is stretched over this lump but is otherwise normal. The mucosal biopsies are normal.
items.explanation: Mallory-Weiss tear Patients present with severe epigastric pain, retching and mild haematemesis. The clinical differential diagnosis includes duodenal perforation, acute pancreatitis, myocardial infarction and oesophageal perforation. Endoscopy confirms the diagnosis, which is self-limiting.

items.stem: There is an ulcerated and polypoidal mass at the lower end of the oesophagus causing obstruction.
items.explanation: Oesophageal varices This may be seen in patients with portal hypertension presenting with haematemesis. The varices are usually injected or banded. More rarely, embolisation or vasopressin may be used. Surgery is almost never indicated nowadays, except in desperate situations.

items.stem: There is evidence of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) and a linear tongue of erythematous mucosa extending for a few centimetres into the oesophagus proximally.
items.explanation: Peptic stricture This is a complication of long-standing GORD. Barrett’s oesophagus may be present. The diagnosis is confirmed on histology, where intestinal metaplasia is seen. Smooth tapering and absence of shouldering differentiate this from malignancy.

items.stem: The gastro-oesophageal junction is at 34 cm with prolapsing fundal mucosa and increased oesophageal fluid. The diaphragm is located at 39 cm.
items.explanation: Rectal cancer Large rectal polyp in an otherwise unfit individual is assessed by taking a detailed history, followed by thorough clinical examination. This is followed by endoscopic assessment and 114 biopsies. If the biopsies show dysplasia, there still may be a focus of cancer. Hence, MRI of pelvis and CT chest abdomen and pelvis are performed. To assess the local T staging, EUS may be beneficial. EUS is used in the lower gastrointestinal tract in the assessment of low rectal polyps to differentiate between T1 and T2 lesions, and in the assessment of perirectal lymph nodes. EUS is also indicated in the assessment of fistula in ano and in assessment of anal sphincter complex in faecal incontinence. However, EUS is an investigation that is operator dependent.

items.stem: A large polypoidal mass is noted in the lower rectum in a patient not fit for major surgery.
items.explanation: Reflux gastritis This is a complication of long-standing GORD. Barrett’s oesophagus may be present. The diagnosis is confirmed on histology, where intestinal metaplasia is seen. Smooth tapering and absence of shouldering differentiate this from malignancy.

items.stem: An 80-year-old man who has just had an OGD after local anaesthetic spray has severe coughing and breathing problems after eating a sandwich in the recovery room.
items.explanation: Local anaesthetic suppresses the gag and swallow reflex. Eating too soon post-endoscopy can cause aspiration pneumonia. Other options like sedation overdose or perforation are less likely in this scenario.

items.stem: A 71-year-old patient collapses and is found to be hypotensive after an endoscopic polypectomy.
items.explanation: Sudden collapse and hypotension following a therapeutic procedure such as polypectomy are classic for post-procedural bleeding. It’s a well-known and immediate risk.

items.stem: A 70-year-old male is rushed to the emergency 8 hours after an endoscopic dilatation of an oesophageal stricture, complaining of severe chest pain and change in voice.
items.explanation: Chest pain, subcutaneous emphysema, or hoarseness post-dilatation are red flags for oesophageal perforation, a life-threatening emergency. This timing and context are critical.

items.stem: An 86-year-old woman has severe pain and bleeding from the mouth following an uneventful OGD.
items.explanation: Older patients with poor dentition are at high risk for dental trauma during scope insertion, particularly if they wear dentures or have brittle teeth. The lack of internal findings suggests an external cause.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman patient has severe bradycardia and low PO2 and is difficult to arouse.
items.explanation: Over-sedation, especially in the elderly, can lead to respiratory depression and bradycardia. Hypoxia and delayed awakening point to a systemic drug effect rather than a procedural complication like perforation.

theme: Abdominal Pain and Masses – Diagnosis Matching
theme_label: Theme 28: Abdominal Pain and Masses – Diagnosis Matching

items.stem: A 58-year-old man complains of a lump in his abdomen deep to an incision for 2 years. This started 3 months after he had an emergency operation for intestinal obstruction when he underwent a right hemicolectomy. The lump is increasing in size and becomes prominent when he coughs and sits up.
items.explanation: The description of a postoperative abdominal lump that increases with coughing or sitting up is characteristic of an incisional hernia, especially following abdominal surgery.

items.stem: A 72-year-old man complains of throbbing backache and a feeling of his heartbeat in his ‘stomach’. On examination a pulsatile mass can be seen in his epigastrium, which looks full.
items.explanation: A pulsatile epigastric mass with backache is a classic presentation of an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The ‘heartbeat in the stomach’ is a hallmark symptom.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman complains of severe colicky abdominal pain of 6 hours duration. It is in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant and radiates to the back. The pain comes and goes, and in between the attacks she is left with a dull ache in the right subcostal region.
items.explanation: Intermittent, colicky pain in the right upper quadrant radiating to the back is typical for biliary colic, usually due to gallstones obstructing the biliary tract.

items.stem: A 74-year-old woman complains of generalised abdominal pain and distension for 36 hours. This started with greenish vomiting, which has now been replaced with brownish faeculent material. She is dehydrated with a distended abdomen and a small tender lump in her right groin of which she is unaware.
items.explanation: Foul, feculent vomiting with abdominal distension and a groin lump suggests a strangulated hernia leading to distal small bowel obstruction. The progression to dehydration supports this diagnosis.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman complains of undue shortness of breath while going about her daily activities. On examination she looks very pale with an irregular non-tender lump in her right iliac fossa.
items.explanation: Chronic anemia, shortness of breath, and a palpable mass in the right iliac fossa are indicative of carcinoma of caecum, which often presents insidiously due to occult blood loss.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man, who admits to being a chronic alcoholic, complains of severe pain in his epigastrium radiating to the back of 8 hours duration. He is sweaty, with a pulse rate of 122 beats per minute, blood pressure of 110/80 mmHg and with a tense, tender abdomen with rigidity.
items.explanation: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back in a chronic alcoholic with systemic distress is highly suggestive of acute pancreatitis.

items.stem: A 70-year-old woman presents with jaundice and vague abdominal pain of 6 weeks duration. On examination she is jaundiced with a long midline scar and an enlarged hard nodular liver. The midline scar is from a left hemicolectomy for carcinoma of the splenic flexure.
items.explanation: Jaundice combined with a history of colectomy and a nodular liver on examination strongly points towards secondary metastases in the liver.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man complains of sudden onset of very severe pain in his epigastrium, radiating to the back, of 6 hours duration. On examination his blood pressure is 130/90 mmHg, pulse rate is 90 beats per minute, the abdominal wall does not move with respiration and he has thoracic respiration. Over the past hour he has been having pain in his right shoulder tip. In the past he has suffered from ‘indigestion’ for a long time.
items.explanation: Sudden, severe epigastric pain with associated shoulder tip pain and a rigid abdomen is characteristic of a perforated duodenal ulcer, likely causing diaphragmatic irritation from free peritoneal air.

theme_label: Theme 29: Diagnoses of Abdominal Wall Hernias

items.stem: A 6-month-old infant has a history of lump over the belly-button that increases in size when the baby cries.
items.explanation: A congenital hernia at the umbilicus in infants is typically an umbilical hernia, exacerbated by crying due to increased intra-abdominal pressure.

items.stem: A 26-year-old presents with a lump over his left groin. Examination reveals cough impulse and a reducible hernia extending into the scrotum. Pressure over the internal ring controls the hernia.
items.explanation: A hernia extending into the scrotum and reducible, controlled at the internal ring, confirms an indirect inguinal hernia, usually congenital.

items.stem: A 60-year-old obese woman has a painful lump just above her umbilicus. Examination confirms a round smooth tender mass with no cough impulse.
items.explanation: A paraumbilical hernia occurs just above the umbilicus and often presents as a tender lump, common in obese women.

items.stem: A 78-year-old woman has a suspected enlarged left groin lymph node. Examination reveals a 2-cm hard, tender and irreducible lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle with no cough impulse.
items.explanation: A lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle is classic for femoral hernia—more common in elderly women, often mistaken for a lymph node.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman describes a gradually increasing lump in the lower, right abdomen. She has had three caesarean sections. There is a Pfannenstiel scar with a reducible mass at its lateral end.
items.explanation: Hernias at the site of previous incisions are incisional hernias. The mass at the lateral end of a Pfannenstiel scar supports this.

items.stem: A 76-year-old man has a 2-year history of small swellings in both groins, causing no real discomfort. Examination confirms reducible hernias, which are not controlled by pressure over the deep inguinal ring.
items.explanation: Bilateral, painless, reducible groin swellings not controlled at the internal ring are characteristic of direct inguinal hernias, common in older men.

items.stem: A 50-year-old man presents with a lump below but well lateral to the umbilicus. You suspect an inguinal hernia but the mass seems to be slightly too high and too lateral for this diagnosis.
items.explanation: A hernia lateral to the rectus muscle, near the semilunar line, indicates a Spigelian hernia—a rare type often confused with inguinal hernias.

items.stem: A 22-year-old fit male presents with a tender, firm, 2-cm nodule in the midline just below the xiphisternum. There is no cough impulse. The patient believes that the lump increases in size on exercise.
items.explanation: Small, tender midline lumps between the xiphisternum and umbilicus are epigastric hernias, often fat-containing and more prominent with exertion.

items.stem: A 62-year-old labourer is referred with an abdominal hernia. When lying down, no mass is visible but on raising his head from the bed, a broadly based swelling appears between the xiphisternum and umbilicus.
items.explanation: A midline separation of the rectus muscles (divarication of recti) presents as a visible ridge when the patient raises his head, rather than a true hernia.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman has a 3-cm firm mass at the umbilicus. She had a laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2 years ago.
items.explanation: Post-laparoscopic surgery hernias at trocar sites (especially at the umbilicus) are known as port-site hernias.

theme_label: Theme 30: Treatment of Abdominal Wall Hernias
options: Laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair (TEP or TAPP)

items.stem: Uncomplicated primary unilateral inguinal hernia.
Recurrent inguinal hernia – post-open repair.
Infantile umbilical hernia.
Recurrent inguinal hernia – post-laparoscopic repair.
Divarication of recti.
Complex incisional hernia in patient known to have extensive adhesions.
Small paraumbilical hernia.

theme: Named Operations and Techniques in Hernia Surgery
theme_label: Theme 31: Named Operations and Techniques in Hernia Surgery

items.stem: Suture repair of inguinal hernia with double breasting of posterior wall of inguinal canal.
Open pre-peritoneal mesh repair for complex inguinal hernia.
Suture repair of paraumbilical hernia with double breasting of anterior sheath.
Suture repair of inguinal hernia employing external oblique aponeurosis.
Open mesh repair of inguinal hernia.
Muscle release to aid abdominal wall closure in large incisional hernia.

A 68-year-old woman complains of recurrent cough that is worse at night when she is woken up from her sleep. She is embarrassed by halitosis. Her general practitioner (GP) has treated her for chest infection several times with antibiotics. Examination shows some signs of basal pneumonitis.
items.explanation: A pharyngeal (Zenker’s) diverticulum can collect food and fluid, leading to regurgitation, halitosis, aspiration at night, and recurrent chest infections. The nocturnal cough and malodour strongly support this diagnosis.

items.stem: A 48-year-old man complains of intermittent dysphagia for almost 1 year. He has some postprandial discomfort, which is relieved by belching and occasional regurgitation of food. This is associated with retrosternal pain and pressure sensation. An ECG is normal. Chest x-ray shows a gas bubble behind the heart.
items.explanation: Rolling (para-oesophageal) hernia presents with postprandial fullness, regurgitation, and a posterior mediastinal gas shadow (gas bubble) on imaging. It may mimic GORD but often lacks typical reflux symptoms like heartburn.

items.stem: A 42-year-old man complains of dysphagia with retrosternal chest pain. This has been intermittent. On one occasion the pain was very severe with pain radiating along the arms. He was admitted as an emergency to the medical ward where his ECG and cardiac enzymes were normal.
items.explanation: Sudden, severe chest pain radiating to the arms with normal cardiac workup points to diffuse oesophageal spasm, which can mimic angina. Dysphagia and non-cardiac chest pain are key features.

items.stem: A 72-year-old man, a long-standing smoker, complains of progressive dysphagia with food sticking behind his mid-sternum for 3 months. The problem started with solids, but now he has difficulty with liquids. He has lost 14 kg of weight during this time. On examination the weight loss is obvious from his loose, ill-fitting clothes.
items.explanation: Progressive dysphagia from solids to liquids, significant weight loss, and age/smoking history are classic for oesophageal carcinoma. The mid-sternal location suggests a mid-oesophageal lesion.

items.stem: A 35-year-old man complains of dysphagia of almost 2 years duration. Occasionally he has regurgitation of foul-smelling stale food and frothy sputum. He has been treated for chest infection a few times by his GP. He has lost some weight and looks slightly malnourished.
items.explanation: Long-standing dysphagia with regurgitation of stale food, weight loss, and recurrent chest infections suggests achalasia. In this motor disorder, the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to relax, causing food stasis.

items.stem: A 42-year-old woman complains of retrosternal burning pain, which she refers to as heartburn, epigastric discomfort and repeated regurgitation. Her symptoms are worse after fatty and spicy foods and by stooping. She has also experienced painful swallowing when she felt an acidic taste in her throat. On examination she is obese with signs of chest infection.
items.explanation: Typical heartburn, regurgitation, worse with posture and food, along with acidic taste and odynophagia (painful swallowing), point clearly to GORD. Obesity is a common risk factor.

theme: Gastric and Perigastric Disorders – Diagnosis Matching
theme_label: Theme 33: Gastric and Perigastric Disorders – Diagnosis Matching

items.stem: A 48-year-old man, a heavy smoker, has been admitted with sudden onset of very severe pain in the epigastrium radiating to the back and right shoulder tip of 3 hours duration. His pulse is 88 beats per minute and his blood pressure (BP) is 120/70 mmHg; his abdomen has board-like rigidity and does not move with respiration, which is mainly thoracic.
items.explanation: The sudden, severe epigastric pain, board-like rigidity, and shoulder tip pain (suggesting diaphragmatic irritation) are classic for a perforated duodenal ulcer. Smoking is an important risk factor.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man complains of epigastric pain for 6 months, the pain not related to food. His appetite has been poor and he has lost 10 kg of weight during this period. There was nothing to find in his abdomen except for evidence of weight loss. An OGD showed diffuse mucosal thickening of the entire pylorus with some ulceration. Histology showed lymphoid hyperplasia with lymphoid cells expanding the lamina propria.
items.explanation: Chronic epigastric pain, weight loss, and diffuse mucosal thickening of the pylorus with lymphoid hyperplasia on biopsy point towards gastric lymphoma.

items.stem: An 80-year-old woman presents with severe itching and her relatives noticed that she was becoming yellow over the last couple of months. Recently she has had vomiting, the vomitus not being bile stained. On examination she has lost a considerable amount of weight and has scratch marks all over her body and a smooth globular mass in the right upper quadrant of her abdomen.
items.explanation: Obstructive jaundice with severe pruritus, vomiting of non-bile-stained contents, weight loss, and a palpable RUQ mass (suggesting Courvoisier’s sign) are indicative of periampullary carcinoma.

items.stem: A 69-year-old man presents with acute haematemesis. He has been well until his presentation, except that recently he has had a feeling of early satiety after small amounts of food. An urgent OGD showed a large submucosal mass with an ulcerated area, which was the site of bleeding.
items.explanation: A large submucosal gastric mass with an ulcerated area that bleeds and causes early satiety is characteristic of a leiomyoma of the stomach.

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman complains of epigastric pain on and off for 3 years for which she took medicines from across the counter. Almost 6 months ago she underwent a repeat OGD and biopsy that showed *H. pylori* infection in a gastric ulcer for which she was treated. She was well after that, but recently the pain has returned. Her haemoglobin is 11.9. Repeat OGD shows a 2-cm diameter punched-out ulcer on the lesser curve with overhanging edges.
items.explanation: A recurrent punched-out ulcer on the lesser curve with overhanging edges in a patient with a history of *H. pylori* infection is consistent with a benign gastric ulcer.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man complains of anorexia and weight loss for 3 months. He has intermittent vomiting associated with malaise. On examination he looks anaemic and has a firm mobile mass in the epigastrium and right hypochondrium.
items.explanation: Anorexia, weight loss, intermittent vomiting, anemia, and a firm, mobile mass in the epigastrium/right hypochondrium strongly suggest carcinoma of the stomach.

items.stem: A 35-year-old man, a bus driver, complains of epigastric pain radiating to the back on and off for several months. He has some backache, for which he took some NSAIDs, and occasionally consumes alcohol. Following a bout of drinking, he vomited and the vomitus was streaked with blood.
items.explanation: Epigastric pain radiating to the back, associated with NSAID use, occasional alcohol intake, and minor bleeding in the vomitus suggests acute gastritis.

items.stem: A 60-year-old man complains of incessant vomiting for 2 weeks. The vomitus contains stale food ingested a few days ago. There is no abdominal pain, although many years ago he suffered from prolonged ‘indigestion’ for which he took antacids from across the counter on and off for years. On examination he has sunken eyes, dry tongue and loss of skin turgor, and his epigastrium looks full. While being examined he had an attack of carpo-pedal spasm.
items.explanation: Incessant vomiting of stale food, signs of dehydration, epigastric fullness, and carpo-pedal spasm (due to electrolyte imbalance) indicate gastric outlet obstruction, likely from peptic scarring.

theme_label: Theme 34: Surgical Procedures – Bariatric & Metabolic Surgery

items.stem: A 50-year-old man weighing 105 kg and with a height of 180 cm presents with a history of progressive and poorly controlled diabetes for 15 years. He was shifted from oral hypoglycaemics to insulin but has shown poor compliance to treatment. He is now beginning to have alteration in renal functions and eye changes.
items.explanation: Ileal transposition is a targeted metabolic surgery primarily used in type 2 diabetics with poor glycaemic control and early end-organ damage. It promotes early stimulation of distal ileal hormones (GLP-1), enhancing insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism, even in patients who are not severely obese.

items.stem: A 30-year-old married woman presents with a weight of 110 kg and a height of 155 cm. She has been diabetic for the past 10 years and is on anti-hypertensives for the past 5 years with a need to escalate the doses of both medications.
items.explanation: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is a powerful metabolic and bariatric procedure that offers both restrictive and malabsorptive components. It results in high remission rates for diabetes and hypertension, making it suitable for patients with multiple comorbidities.

items.stem: A 20-year-old man, a college student, presents with a history of weight gain over the past 5 years. He has a BMI of 40 and is particularly worried about his physique. He has tried dieting and exercise, appears well motivated, and wants a safe procedure with regular follow-up.
items.explanation: Gastric banding is ideal for younger, motivated patients seeking a reversible and minimally invasive option. Although it has a lower risk profile, it requires regular follow-up for band adjustments and lifestyle modifications.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman who underwent a sleeve gastrectomy 3 years ago presents with weight regain and relapse of diabetes. She presently has a BMI of 52 and is otherwise fit and healthy.
items.explanation: Bilio-pancreatic diversion (BPD) is the most effective procedure for substantial weight loss and diabetes remission, especially in patients who experience metabolic relapse after previous bariatric procedures. It induces significant malabsorption, which is beneficial in cases of severe obesity.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with a BMI of 45. He has been obese for the past 10 years with no medical comorbidity except for snoring during sleep for the past 1 year.
items.explanation: Sleeve gastrectomy is appropriate for patients with morbid obesity and minimal comorbidities. It effectively reduces weight while preserving the normal intestinal anatomy and has a lower risk of long-term nutritional deficiencies.

theme: Liver and Biliary Disorders – Diagnosis Matching
theme_label: Theme 35: Liver and Biliary Disorders – Diagnosis Matching

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman has a history of recurrent attacks of fever with rigors, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice with itching. Biochemistry shows a jaundice of obstructive nature. CT scan shows intrahepatic ductal dilatation with stones.
items.explanation: — Benign vascular liver lesion, often incidental on ultrasound/CT.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with recurrent episodes of right upper quadrant pain with jaundice. Biochemistry shows an obstructive pattern of jaundice. Five years ago she underwent a panproctocolectomy for ulcerative colitis and has been well since, except for these attacks. ERCP shows irregular narrowed intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts.
items.explanation: — Solitary OCP-related tumor in young women.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman complains of general malaise, lethargy, pruritus and jaundice, the latter being present over the last 3 months. The LFTs show a rise in bilirubin, transaminases and prothrombin time. She has had recurrent small haematemesis and has ascites.
items.explanation: — Congenital intrahepatic duct dilatation with intrahepatic stones and cholangitis.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman complains of abdominal discomfort and distension. She has had three episodes of small haematemesis in the past 6 months. On examination she has hepatomegaly and ascites. All the LFTs are deranged. CT scan of the liver shows a large congested liver.
items.explanation: — Fever, RUQ pain, tender hepatomegaly after travel; anchovy-paste pus.

items.stem: A fit-looking 50-year-old man complains of recent onset of dull aching right upper quadrant pain of 3 to 4 months’ duration. Examination shows no abnormality. Liver function tests are normal, as is an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. An ultrasound of the liver shows a 6 cm solitary cystic lesion.
items.explanation: — Malaise, anorexia, jaundice with raised transaminases.

items.stem: A 25-year-old man complains of generally feeling unwell with fever and weight loss. He has had bloodstained motions on and off for the last 6 weeks after he returned from the Indian subcontinent where he was working for 6 months. On examination he has a tender right upper quadrant with hepatomegaly. Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic cavity in the right lobe with ill-defined borders.
items.explanation: — Benign solitary hepatic cyst with thin wall on imaging.

items.stem: A 50-year-old woman has had recurrent attacks of colicky right upper quadrant and epigastric pain with jaundice, high temperature with rigors and itching. 10 months ago she underwent an uneventful laparoscopic cholecystectomy. On examination she is jaundiced with scratch marks all over her body and hepatomegaly. She has raised serum bilirubin and the ALP is 1100 IU/L. Ultrasound shows a dilated common bile duct with stones.
items.explanation: — Beading strictures of intra/extrahepatic ducts; linked to IBD.

items.stem: A 35-year-old man presents with general ill health, weight loss, anorexia and malaise for several weeks. He has developed jaundice for the last 2 weeks; he has no pruritus. Abdominal examination shows a tender hepatomegaly. Liver function tests show raised bilirubin and transaminases.
items.explanation: — Fever, leukocytosis; multiloculated collection on US/CT.

items.stem: A 75-year-old man, an insulin-dependent diabetic for 40 years, complains of anorexia, fever, malaise and right upper quadrant discomfort. On examination there is weight loss and tender hepatomegaly. Ultrasound shows a multiloculated cystic mass, a finding confirmed on CT scan.
items.explanation: — Middle-aged woman, pruritus, cholestatic LFTs, antimitochondrial antibodies.

items.stem: A 50-year-old man, a native of Cyprus, presents with a painful mass in the right upper quadrant. The pain is a continuous dull ache and has the features of a mass arising from the right lobe of the liver. The blood count shows eosinophilia. CT scan shows a smooth space-occupying lesion with multiple septa within it.
items.explanation: — Hepatic venous outflow obstruction causing painful hepatomegaly and ascites.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman who is on the contraceptive pill presents with right upper quadrant aching pain. She is fit without any physical findings. Her LFTs and other blood tests are normal. Ultrasound of the liver shows a single well-demarcated hyperechoic mass and CT scan demonstrates a well-circumscribed vascular solid tumour.
items.explanation: — Charcot triad ± Reynolds pentad; urgent biliary decompression.

items.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with dull, persistent upper abdominal pain, weakness, weight loss and occasional fever. He had one episode of haematemesis. Abdominal examination shows an enlarged liver with a mass in the right lobe. Liver function tests show elevation of the transaminases and much-raised alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
items.explanation: — Echinococcus cyst with septations; exposure to dogs/sheep.

items.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with dragging pain in the right upper quadrant for 3 months and weight loss. On examination he is slightly jaundiced. He has an enlarged liver. Three years ago he underwent a right hemicolectomy for cancer of the caecum. Liver function tests show elevation of all the parameters. Ultrasound shows a solid mass in the right lobe, and a CECT confirms the mass with lack of enhancement.
items.explanation: — Multiple/solitary lesions in patient with prior colorectal cancer.

items.stem: In a 30-year-old woman, during laparoscopic cholecystectomy, the surgeon noticed that the under-surface of the liver has several lesions that are blue in colour.
items.explanation: — Hypervascular lesion with central scar on CECT/MRI.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman underwent an ultrasound for suspected biliary pain. The ultrasound of the biliary tract was normal but showed a solid lesion in the liver. A subsequent CECT scan showed a vascular lesion surrounding a solid mass with central scarring.
items.explanation: ) — Weight loss, RUQ mass, high AFP; risk with chronic hepatitis/cirrhosis.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man with a history of gallstones presents in A&E with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and vomiting.
items.explanation: B. Acute pancreatitis: classic severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, often due to gallstones.

items.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with sharp left loin and left upper quadrant pain radiating to the groin. He is not jaundiced.
items.explanation: K. Renal colic: severe, colicky loin pain radiating to the groin, typically with nausea.

items.stem: A 44-year-old woman presents with continuous right upper quadrant pain, vomiting and fever. There is marked right upper quadrant tenderness when palpating on inspiration.
items.explanation: F. Acute cholecystitis: positive Murphy’s sign with right upper quadrant tenderness.

items.stem: A 26-year-old male with a previous history of abdominal surgery presents with colicky central abdominal pain rapidly followed by production of copious bilestained vomitus.
items.explanation: E. Small bowel obstruction: early vomiting with progressive abdominal distension.

items.stem: A 50-year-old man with a history of epigastric pain presents with constant severe generalized abdominal pain. On examination he is distressed and has a rigid abdomen. Pulse is 110/min, BP 100/60 mmHg.“
items.explanation: C. Perforated viscus: rigid abdomen indicating peritonitis.

items.stem: A 21-year-old student presents with diffuse cramping abdominal pain with alternating constipation and diarrhoea; colonoscopy and inflammatory markers are normal.
items.explanation: B. Irritable bowel syndrome: diagnosis of exclusion in young patients with alternating bowel habits.

items.stem: A 9-year-old girl presents with fever, nausea and right iliac fossa pain that initially started around the belly button.
items.explanation: J. Acute appendicitis: typical shift of pain from the periumbilical region to the right iliac fossa.

items.stem: A 35-year-old man presents with weight loss, diarrhoea, abdominal pain and aphthous mouth ulcers; a mass is palpable in the right Blood tests reveal low serum B12 and folate. “iliac fossa.
items.explanation: H. Crohn’s disease: chronic inflammatory process with systemic features such as weight loss and oral ulcers.

items.stem: A 72-year-old man with a history of constipation presents with increased temperature, diarrhoea and left iliac fossa pain. On examination there is tenderness in the left iliac fossa.“
items.explanation: M. Diverticulitis: inflammation of colonic diverticula typically in the sigmoid colon.

items.stem: A 55-year-old patient with several months of epigastric discomfort presents acutely with free gas under the diaphragm on x-ray.
items.explanation: L. Perforated duodenal ulcer: free gas under the diaphragm indicates gastrointestinal perforation.

items.stem: An elderly constipated woman’s x-ray shows a dilated ‘inverted U’ loop of bowel.
items.explanation: G. Sigmoid volvulus: twisting of the sigmoid colon commonly seen in elderly patients.

items.stem: A 31-year-old man presents with fever, bloody diarrhoea and a colonic dilatation of 8 cm with loss of haustral pattern.
items.explanation: I. Ulcerative colitis: radiological loss of haustra with colonic dilatation.

items.stem: A 26-year-old student presents with bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain and weight loss; barium enema shows ‘cobblestoning’ and strictures.
items.explanation: A. Crohn’s disease: barium enema features include cobblestoning and strictures.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with severe epigastric pain and vomiting; x-ray reveals an absent psoas shadow and a ‘sentinel loop’ of proximal jejunum.
items.explanation: D. Acute pancreatitis: the ‘sentinel loop’ suggests localized ileus near the inflamed pancreas.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with fever and significant right upper quadrant pain. On examination, there is marked jaundice and the nurse has reported that the patient is having rigors. Blood tests show plasma bilirubin 250 mmol/L, ALT 200 U/L, ALP 800 U/L, WCC 23 × 10⁹.
items.explanation: E Ascending cholangitis: Ascending cholangitis usually occurs secondary to bacterial contamination of an obstructed biliary system. The classical description (fever with rigors, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice – Charcot’s triad) mandates urgent management with antibiotics and biliary decompression.

items.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with constant right upper quadrant pain associated with vomiting. He is afebrile.
items.explanation: A Biliary colic: Biliary colic is the result of gallbladder spasm due to a stone lodged in Hartmann’s pouch or the cystic duct.

items.stem: A 63-year-old man presents with a 3-day history of worsening abdominal pain and vomiting. Abdominal x-ray reveals dilated loops of small bowel and air in the biliary tree.
items.explanation: D Gallstone ileus: Gallstone ileus is caused by mechanical obstruction from a gallstone that enters the bowel via a fistula.

items.stem: A 52-year-old man presents with vomiting and severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Abdominal x-ray shows a dilated proximal small bowel loop.
items.explanation: C Acute pancreatitis: Acute pancreatitis in this context is due to pancreatic duct obstruction with subsequent enzyme activation.

theme_label: Theme 40: Management of inflammatory bowel disease

items.stem: A 65-year-old patient suffering from frequent debilitating exacerbations of ulcerative colitis who desires curative surgery.
items.explanation: F Proctocolectomy with ileostomy: A curative procedure removing the entire diseased colon, resulting in a permanent end stoma.

items.stem: A 28-year-old patient with ulcerative colitis refractory to medical therapy who agrees on surgery but does not want a stoma.
items.explanation: E Proctocolectomy with ileal pouch: Allows pouch formation to avoid a permanent stoma in young patients.

items.stem: A 30-year-old patient with ulcerative colitis presents to A&E with severe abdominal pain and is diagnosed with toxic megacolon.
items.explanation: H Subtotal colectomy and ileostomy: The emergency procedure for toxic megacolon in acutely inflamed bowel.

items.stem: A 28-year-old patient with Crohn’s disease presents with complete small bowel obstruction; small bowel follow-through shows short strictures.
items.explanation: C Stricturoplasty: A bowel-conserving procedure for short strictures in Crohn’s disease.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man is found to have a rectal carcinoma invading the anal sphincter.
items.explanation: H Abdominoperineal resection: The operation of choice for low rectal tumours when sphincter preservation is not feasible.

items.stem: A 6 A 69-year-old man is brought to A&E with an acute abdomen. He is resuscitated and then taken to theatre for explorative laparotomy. He is found to have a perforated sigmoid colon secondary to a mass with malignant features.
items.explanation: C Hartmann’s procedure: Involves resection of the diseased sigmoid colon with formation of an end colostomy, used in emergency perforated cases.

items.stem: A 49-year-old man with weight loss and anaemia of unknown origin is found to have a large caecal tumour on colonoscopy.
items.explanation: A Right hemicolectomy: Standard treatment for caecal tumours ensuring oncological clearance.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man with fresh rectal bleeding is diagnosed with a tumour in the middle third of the rectum.
items.explanation: D Anterior resection: Preferred for mid-rectal tumours with total mesorectal excision.

items.stem: A 42-year-old alcoholic presents with haematemesis.
items.explanation: G Oesophagogastroduodenoscopy: Allows visualization of the upper GI tract to identify sources of bleeding (e.g. varices).

items.stem: A 65-year-old man presents with weight loss, diarrhoea, and He has noticed blood mixed in with stools..
items.explanation: I Colonoscopy: Enables direct visualization and biopsy in suspected right-sided colonic lesions.

items.stem: A 74-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of worsening constipation and rectal bleeding.
items.explanation: B Flexible sigmoidoscopy: Best for evaluating left-sided colonic lesions.

items.stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of diverticular disease is admitted with suspected diverticulitis He has been treated with antibiotics and intravenous fluids but is not improving after 24 hours.“
items.explanation: E CT abdomen: Helps detect complications of diverticulitis such as abscess formation.

items.stem: A 54-year-old woman presents to A&E with a 48-hour history of colicky abdominal pain, vomiting and abdominal distension. Basic observations on arrival are: pulse 120/min, BP 100/75 mmHg, temperature 38°C. Abdominal examination reveals generalized tenderness, with a firm, tender, 3 ! 4 cm swelling in the right groin. Bowel sounds are absent.
items.explanation: B Strangulated inguinal hernia: Indicates vascular compromise of entrapped bowel needing urgent surgery.

items.stem: A 13-year-old boy underwent an appendicectomy 7 days ago for a suppurative appendicitis. Over the past 48 hours he has complained of right iliac fossa pain, vomiting and abdominal distension. Bowel sounds are absent. Basic observations on arrival are: pulse 110/min, BP 105/64 mmHg, temperature 37.2°C. His mother is a nurse and says that he has had spiking temperatures of above 38°C at home.
items.explanation: G Intra-abdominal abscess: A complication post appendicectomy causing paralytic ileus.

items.stem: A 76-year-old man with a history of hemicolectomy 3 years ago presents to his GP with worsening colicky abdominal pain associated with vomiting, and abdominal distension. Basic observations on arrival are: pulse 98/min, BP 165/75 mmHg, temperature 37.8°C. On abdominal examination there is a distended abdomen with no tenderness, rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds are tinkling.
items.explanation: A Adhesions: The most common cause of obstruction in patients with previous surgery.

items.stem: A 23-year-old man with a 6-month history of weight loss, anorexia, recurrent abdominal pain after eating, and diarrhoea presents to A&E. The pain is colicky associated with vomiting, absolute constipation, and abdominal distension over the past 3 days. Basic observations on arrival are: pulse 120/min, BP 89/56 mmHg, temperature 38.2°C. He is tender in the central abdominal region without guarding or rebound. Blood tests: Hb 10.1 g/dL, WCC 18.0 ! 109 /L, CRP 155, Alb 28.
items.explanation: D Crohn’s disease: Chronic inflammatory changes may lead to stricture formation and obstruction.

lead: 1 A 65-year-old man collapses in the street. On examination he has an abdominal
mass lying above the umbilicus that is expansile and pulsatile.
2 A 75-year-old man with a 3-month history of dyspepsia presents with weight loss
and abdominal distension. On examination, a 3.5-cm, hard, irregular tender epi-
gastric mass can be felt which moves on respiration. Percussion of the distended
abdomen reveals shifting dullness. The left supraclavicular node is palpable.
3 A 70-year-old woman presents with a mass in the right iliac fossa and severe
microcytic anaemia. On examination the mass is firm, irregular and 4 cm in
diameter. The lower edge is palpable.
4 A 35-year-old woman is worried about an abdominal mass that has grown over
the last 6 months and a similar length history of very heavy menstrual bleeding
with no intermenstrual bleeding. On examination, a knobbly mass can be felt in
the middle lower quadrant that is dull to percussion. The lower edge is not
palpable. She is otherwise well.
5 A 70-year-old alcoholic presents with a tender upper abdominal mass. CT shows a
thick-walled, rounded, fluid-filled mass adjacent to the pancreas.
unparsed: 1. K. Abdominal aortic aneurysm — Expansile, pulsatile epigastric mass above the umbilicus in a collapsed 65-year-old man.
2. C. Gastric carcinoma — Epigastric hard mass that moves with respiration, weight loss, ascites, and left supraclavicular (Virchow) node.
3. I. Caecal carcinoma — Firm right iliac fossa mass with severe microcytic anemia from chronic occult bleeding.
4. E. Fibroids — Enlarging, knobbly, non-palpable lower edge uterine mass with heavy menstrual bleeding.
5. F. Pancreatic pseudocyst — Tender upper abdominal mass in an alcoholic; CT shows thick-walled fluid collection near the pancreas.

items.stem: A 28-year-old man with Crohn’s disease complains of watery discharge from a puckered area 2cm from the anal canal.
items.explanation: E Fistula-in-ano: Common in Crohn’s disease; management is initially conservative with antibiotics and drainage if abscess forms.

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman who has recently given birth complains of excrutiating pain on defecation that persists for hours afterwards. Rectal examination is not possible due to pain.
items.explanation: A Anal fissure: Causes excruciating pain on defecation due to extreme tenderness.

items.stem: A 30-year-old taxi driver complains of tenderness from an area in the midline of the natal cleft about 4 cm above the anus. This problem has been remitting and recurring for 2 years and has started to discharge today for the first time.
items.explanation: F Pilonidal abscess: Occurs in the midline natal cleft, often presenting with recurrent discharge.

items.stem: A 27-year-old pregnant woman presents with constipation and bright red blood coating her stools. On examination, two bluish tender spongy masses are found protruding from the anus. These do not reduce spontaneously and require digital reduction.
items.explanation: K Third-degree haemorrhoids: Prolapsed haemorrhoids requiring digital reduction.

items.stem: A 19-year-old woman presents with multiple papilliferous lesions around the anus.”
items.explanation: B Perianal warts: Caused by HPV infection, presenting as multiple papilliferous lesions.

unparsed: X
