items.stem: A 68-year-old man complains of increasing dysphagia of 3 months duration. He is unable to swallow any solids, and liquids go down with difficulty. He has lost 25 kilogrammes in weight during this period. What should be the first investigation?
items.explanation: This patient likely has an oesophageal carcinoma. After initial diagnosis via OGD, EUS is preferred before biopsy as it provides high-resolution images for assessing local invasion and nearby lymph node involvement. Performing biopsy first may distort the tissue planes and interfere with ultrasound interpretation.

items.stem: A 78-year-old man complains of gnawing backache associated with urinary frequency and poor stream for 4 months. Transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) biopsy showed a carcinoma of prostate.
items.explanation: This patient has confirmed prostate cancer with symptoms suggesting bony metastases. A radionuclide bone scan is ideal for detecting skeletal metastases, offering full-body imaging to assess for spread, even before radiographic changes occur.

items.stem: A 32-year-old man while skiing sustained an injury to his right ankle following which it became very painful and grossly deformed.
items.explanation: The most appropriate initial imaging for a suspected fracture-dislocation is a plain x-ray, but only after emergency reduction and splinting to avoid further soft tissue injury or neurovascular compromise. Imaging prior to reduction delays treatment and increases complication risk.

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman sustained a blunt injury to her lower chest and upper abdomen while horse riding. She was brought in with hypovolaemic shock. Having been resuscitated according to the ATLS protocol, she is now stable.
items.explanation: In a stable post-resuscitation trauma patient, CECT is the ideal imaging tool to assess intra-abdominal and thoracic injuries. It provides detailed cross-sectional anatomy and can identify solid organ damage, bleeding, and other critical pathologies quickly and comprehensively.

items.stem: A 70-year-old man is undergoing a laparotomy for liver resection for metastases from colorectal carcinoma.
items.explanation: IOS provides real-time high-resolution imaging of the liver during surgery, detecting small metastases that might be missed by preoperative scans. It ensures complete lesion clearance in liver resections for colorectal metastases.

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman presented with a lymph nodal lump over her right supraclavicular area. Excision biopsy showed a non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma.
items.explanation: PET/CT is used for staging lymphoma, identifying metabolically active disease and occult involvement. It provides both functional and anatomical detail, essential for treatment planning and monitoring response.

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman has been admitted as an emergency with right upper quadrant pain, pyrexia and vomiting. On examination she is toxic, with a positive Murphy’s sign.
items.explanation: This is classic for acute cholecystitis. Abdominal ultrasound is the first-line investigation to evaluate gallbladder inflammation, gallstones, and bile duct dilatation. It is non-invasive, quick, and sensitive for gallbladder pathology.

items.stem: A 62-year-old man presented with a large soft-tissue mass on the medial aspect of his left femoral triangle of 4 months duration. The mass is hard, immobile and tender.
items.explanation: This presentation raises concern for a soft tissue sarcoma. MRI is the gold standard for soft tissue tumour imaging, providing excellent contrast resolution and anatomical detail for local staging and surgical planning.

items.stem: A 29-year-old man is admitted to the surgical ward following an acute exacerbation of Crohn’s disease. He had a limited small bowel resection several months ago and has subsequently developed a high enterocutaneous fistula. On examination he appears malnourished.
items.explanation: The patient with an enterocutaneous fistula and inflamed bowel secondary to Crohn’s disease is unlikely to absorb enteral feeds; hence, TPN is indicated.

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman is involved in a road traffic accident and suffers significant head injuries with associated maxillofacial trauma. A prolonged recovery is expected.
items.explanation: In the presence of maxillofacial trauma, it is unsafe to insert a nasogastric/nasojejunal tube so PEG feeding is the best alternative for a prolonged recovery.

items.stem: A 57-year-old man with oesophageal cancer is severely malnourished due to significant dysphagia to solid food. He is able to tolerate small volumes of liquid feed with discomfort.
items.explanation: Severe dysphagia due to oesophageal cancer precludes oral solid intake; bypassing the obstruction via a nasogastric tube (enteral feeding) is optimal.

items.stem: A 25-year-old homeless patient who has not eaten for 24 hours requires, later in the day, an incision and drainage procedure for a groin abscess.
items.explanation: For a patient scheduled for a minor procedure with short-term fasting, avoidance of enteral feeding with IV fluid supplementation is appropriate.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man presents with a swelling over his medial right thigh. On examination, the swelling is slightly tender and pulsatile but the patient otherwise feels well. The patient admits injecting heroin into the area earlier in the day.
items.explanation: A pulsatile thigh swelling after injection suggests a false femoral aneurysm.

items.stem: An 18-year-old man presents to the emergency department after developing mild pain in the left testicle while playing football. On examination, the left testicle is larger and more irregular compared with the right.
items.explanation: Unilateral irregular testicular enlargement is suspicious for testicular tumour.

items.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left testicle. On examination, there is a whitish discharge at the urethral meatus and the scrotum is swollen and tender to palpation.
items.explanation: Urethral discharge with scrotal tenderness indicates epididymo-orchitis.

items.stem: A 37-year-old man presents with a painless swelling in his groin. On examination, the swelling is fluctuant, non-tender, and non-pulsatile. The patient does, however, admit to some tenderness in his back. He is currently taking rifampicin and isoniazid for a “chest infection.”
items.explanation: Groin swelling with back tenderness in a TB patient suggests psoas abscess.

items.stem: A 13-year-old boy presents with sudden-onset, severe pain in his left testicle, accompanied by lower abdominal pain and vomiting. On examination, the testicle is swollen, erythematous, and very tender to palpation. The left testicle is in its normal anatomical position.
items.explanation: Acute scrotal pain, swelling, and tenderness in a young boy confirm testicular torsion.

items.stem: A 28-year-old man presents with a large left-sided scrotal swelling that is causing slight discomfort. On examination, the swelling is soft but does not transilluminate. You cannot get above it, and it disappears on lying flat; however, there is no cough impulse.
items.explanation: Varicoceles are typically soft, reduce on lying down, and are most common on the left side. The inability to get above the swelling and absence of transillumination support this diagnosis.

items.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with a swelling in his right scrotum that has been increasing in size over the last year. On examination, the swelling is non-tender, fluctuant, and it transilluminates. It is possible to get above the swelling, but the testis is not palpable.
items.explanation: A hydrocele is an accumulation of serous fluid in the scrotum, with transillumination and a fluctuant, non-tender mass where the testis may not be separately palpable.

items.stem: A 64-year-old man presents with a small lump on the skin of his left scrotum. On examination, the lump is tethered to the skin but not attached to any underlying structure, and it is not tender.
items.explanation: Sebaceous cysts are benign, superficial lesions tethered to the dermis and typically non-tender.

items.stem: A 7-year-old boy who has been admitted to hospital with viral meningitis acutely develops a painful swelling in his testicle. On examination, the boy is pyrexial and the swelling is tender.
items.explanation: Mumps orchitis is a complication of mumps infection causing a painful, tender testicular swelling with systemic signs.

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with a swelling on her left thigh, below and lateral to the pubic tubercle. On examination, the swelling is bluish, non-tender, non-pulsatile, and compressible. The patient is otherwise well.
items.explanation: A saphena varix is a venous swelling near the saphenofemoral junction that is bluish, compressible, and located below and lateral to the pubic tubercle.

items.stem: A 27-year-old man presents after haematemesis with four episodes of vomiting. He is drowsy, pulse 96/min, BP 130/70 mmHg, urine output 60 mL in the first hour.

items.stem: A 54-year-old man with calf erythema and pain has HR 120/min, BP 100/65 mmHg, RR 30/min, T 38.5°C.
items.explanation: Septic shock presents with fever, tachycardia, hypotension in infection.

items.stem: A 67-year-old diabetic presents feeling unwell. He is cool and clammy with elevated JVP, pulse 110/min, BP 90/50 mmHg.
items.explanation: Cool, clammy skin and raised JVP indicate cardiogenic shock.

items.stem: A 24-year-old man after RTA with bilateral femoral fractures appears pale, pulse 130/min, BP 80/58 mmHg, RR 30/min, urine output 30 mL over 3 hours.
items.explanation: Tachycardia, hypotension, and oliguria reflect Class III hypovolaemic shock.

items.stem: A 42-year-old woman after RTA suddenly becomes faint; peripheries are warm and dry, pulse 40/min, BP 82/48 mmHg.
items.explanation: Bradycardia with warm, dry peripheries indicates neurogenic shock.

items.stem: A 47-year-old woman with a 3 cm firm breast lump fixed to skin.
items.explanation: CA 15-3 is used in monitoring breast cancer.

items.stem: A 76-year-old man with new-onset constipation, fresh blood in stools, and weight loss.
items.explanation: CEA is a marker for colorectal cancer.

items.stem: A 68-year-old man with difficulty passing urine and dribbling.
items.explanation: PSA is the marker for prostate pathology.

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman with an irregular, pigmented 1 cm lesion on her leg that itches and bleeds.
items.explanation: S-100 is used in melanoma evaluation.

items.stem: A 62-year-old woman with painless progressive jaundice and a palpable gallbladder.
items.explanation: CA 19-9 is associated with pancreaticobiliary malignancies.

items.stem: A 67-year-old man presents with difficulty passing urine. He has an elevated prostate-specific antigen, and a transrectal biopsy is performed.
items.explanation: Gleason score grades prostate cancer.

items.stem: A 72-year-old man has a sigmoid tumour resected. The pathologist notes that the tumour is confined to the bowel wall and that there is no lymph node involvement.

items.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with a 4-week history of fever, night sweats and itching. He has lost 5 kg in weight over the last fortnight. On examination, enlarged lymph nodes are palpable in the neck.

items.stem: A 65-year-old woman has a colon tumour resected successfully. The pathology report states that the tumour has invaded the bowel wall. The preoperative CT scan shows multiple metastases in the liver.
items.explanation: Dukes D denotes distant metastases.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman presents with an irregularly pigmented lesion on her lower right leg that is subsequently excised.
items.explanation: Breslow thickness stages melanoma.

A 62-year-old woman develops discomfort of the right lower leg 7 days after a hysterectomy for carcinoma of the uterus. On examination, she has a pyrexia of 37.5°C and bilateral ankle oedema (right > left).
items.explanation: .- Wound infection (J) typically appears around day 5+ with local signs of infection. - Pseudo-obstruction (H) presents as acute colonic distension without a mechanical cause. - Atelectasis (A) usually occurs within 48 hours post-op, causing reduced oxygen saturations. - Anastomotic dehiscence (B) often presents 3–7 days post-op with peritonitis and sepsis. - DVT (D) often presents several days post-op with calf discomfort, swelling, and sometimes fever.

items.stem: A 72-year-old woman has been admitted for a mastectomy. She gives a history of well-controlled hypertension for which she is on medication. On examination she looks well, and the examination of the cardiovascular system reveals an ejection systolic murmur in the aortic area.
A 50-year-old woman is admitted for a routine repair of a femoral hernia. She has chronic asthma for which she has been taking medication on a regular basis, but it is not always well controlled.

A 76-year-old patient is admitted as an emergency with symptoms of obstructive jaundice. An ultrasound shows the presence of a gallstone in the common bile duct. She is about to undergo an endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography.

A 66-year-old man is admitted for a coronary artery bypass operation. During routine clerking, he describes an episode when he temporarily lost the vision in his right eye and some weakness of his arm, which has now recovered completely.
items.explanation: - Echocardiogram (G) clarifies a suspected aortic stenosis. - Spirometry (J) is crucial for assessing poorly controlled asthma. - Clotting screen (E) is required with obstructive jaundice before ERCP. - Carotid Doppler (C) checks for stenosis if TIA symptoms are present.

items.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with a tense lump in the scrotum which has appeared over the last 3 weeks and is mildly tender. It is transilluminable and the testis cannot be felt separately.
A 22-year-old man presents with a tender lump in his scrotum that his girlfriend noticed in the shower. He has lost a stone in weight over the last 2 months, and clinically, there is a lump attached.

A 30-year-old man presents with a large lump in the scrotum that came on a few days ago. It is large, tense and you cannot feel above it. It is nontender and non-transilluminable, and it has a cough impulse.
A 35-year-old man presents with a left-sided lump in the scrotum. He says that it disappears when he lies down. Upon palpation, the lump is inconsistent in nature and feels very mobile.
items.explanation: - Hydrocele (C) is fluid around the testis, transilluminable, testis not felt separately. - Testicular tumour (I) often presents as a painless or mildly tender swelling, may have systemic symptoms. - Indirect inguinal hernia (E) descends into the scrotum, has a cough impulse, not transilluminable. - Varicocele (J) feels like a “bag of worms” and disappears on lying flat.
